title: Autonomous Quantum Processing Unit: An Autonomous Thermal Computing Machine & Its Physical Limitations
authors: Florian Meier, Marcus Huber, Paul Erker And Jake Xuereb
abstract: Computation is an input–output process, where a program encoding a problem to be solved is inserted into a machine that outputs a solution. Quantum computation conventionally relies on classical, external control outside the quantum computer to execute a program, obscuring computational and thermodynamic resources required. To understand the fundamental limits of computation, however, it is pivotal to work with a fully self-contained description of a quantum computation modeling the resources on the same footing as the computation itself. By developing a framework that we dub the autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) we model quantum computation in the framework of autonomous thermal machines. Consisting of an internal quantum timekeeping mechanism, instruction register and memory system the aQPU allows investigating relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed and fidelity of a desired quantum computation.
tldr: This paper introduces an autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) that models quantum computation as a thermal machine, enabling the study of thermodynamic costs and physical limitations of computation.
motivation: Conventional quantum computation relies on external classical control, obscuring the fundamental thermodynamic and computational resources required. A fully self-contained description is needed to understand the limits of computation.
method: The authors develop a framework for an autonomous Quantum Processing Unit (aQPU) that includes an internal quantum clock, instruction register, and memory, treating computation as a process within autonomous thermal machines.
result: The aQPU framework allows investigation of relationships between thermodynamic cost, complexity, speed, and fidelity of quantum computations, revealing physical limitations.
conclusion: Modeling quantum computation as an autonomous thermal machine provides insights into the fundamental resources and constraints, advancing the understanding of the thermodynamics of computation.

title: Spin-induced Multipartite Steady-state Entanglement Of Motional Modes In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Membranes
authors: Nahid Yazdi, Vahid Salari, Roohollah Ghobadi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we focus on a scheme in which three high-quality-factor mechanical modes of a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) membrane monolayer are coupled to a common optically addressable spin defect present in the membrane via magnetic field interaction. We show that this coupling induces an effective phonon-phonon interaction in the dispersive regime and under appropriate magnetic field and microwave modulation. We derive the Langevin-Heisenberg equations of motion for vibrational modes to analyze optimal parameter regimes for reaching a physically stable system. We also investigate the effect of coupling strength on purity and entanglement. Our results demonstrate that bipartite and genuinely tripartite steady-state entanglement between different vibrational modes of hBN may be achieved in a broad spectrum of experimental parameters. This study has the potential to enable scalability to be implemented for the generation of two-dimensional continuous-variable cluster states for universal quantum computation.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate multipartite steady-state entanglement between mechanical modes of a hexagonal boron nitride membrane via coupling to an optically addressable spin defect.
motivation: Generating multipartite entanglement in solid-state systems is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks.
method: The authors model three mechanical modes of an hBN membrane coupled to a spin defect via magnetic field, derive Langevin-Heisenberg equations, and analyze parameter regimes for stability and entanglement.
result: Bipartite and genuinely tripartite steady-state entanglement between vibrational modes can be achieved over a broad range of experimental parameters.
conclusion: This scheme could enable scalable generation of two-dimensional continuous-variable cluster states for universal quantum computation.

title: Phonon Heat Transport With Squeezing-based Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yan Cao, Cheng Yang, Xintong Gu, Shenzhu Wang, Jiteng Sheng, Haibin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The controllability of phonon thermal transport is fundamental for numerous technologies, from cooling high-performance chips to managing heat in quantum computing. Despite extensive efforts, on-demand, real-time control of phonon heat flow remains elusive, being fundamentally constrained by the temperature gradient. Here we achieve this long-sought phonon heat transport by introducing a novel mechanism using quantum squeezing in a cavity optomechanical system. We find that phonon squeezing of near-ground-state mechanical resonators via an optomechanically induced parametric process breaks the continuous U(1) rotation symmetry in phase space, and consequently the symmetry in the heat current structure. We reveal that heat flow under a constant temperature gradient can be deterministically amplified, reduced, or even reversed, a capability previously unattainable. With phonon squeezing, we achieve over twentyfold amplification of heat flow and reversal within 30 milliseconds. Importantly, quantum discord analysis reveals a direct connection between heat flow reversal and quantum correlation. Our results establish quantum squeezing as a versatile platform for on-demand phononic thermal control, opening avenues for active heat management in quantum devices and thermal logic circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates on-demand control of phonon heat transport using quantum squeezing in a cavity optomechanical system, achieving amplification, reduction, and reversal of heat flow under a constant temperature gradient.
motivation: Real-time control of phonon heat flow is crucial for thermal management in quantum devices and computing, but has been fundamentally limited by the temperature gradient.
method: The authors introduce quantum squeezing via an optomechanically induced parametric process to break the U(1) rotation symmetry in phase space, enabling control over heat current symmetry.
result: They achieve over twentyfold amplification of heat flow and reversal within 30 milliseconds, with quantum discord analysis linking heat flow reversal to quantum correlations.
conclusion: Quantum squeezing provides a versatile platform for on-demand phononic thermal control, opening avenues for active heat management in quantum devices and thermal logic circuits.

title: Theory Of Approximate Quantum Error Correction And The Error-set Model
authors: Dor Elimelech, Victor V. Albert, Alexander Barg
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of approximate quantum error correction (QEC) based on the error-set model, complemented by general methods for code construction. Exact QEC has a powerful error-set structure: by the Knill-Laflamme conditions, a code correcting a given error set automatically protects against every channel whose Kraus operators lie in their linear span. This linearity gives rise to code distance, the equivalence between erasures and general errors, and a theory of asymptotically good codes. A longstanding view has been that these features do not extend to AQEC, leaving the theory essentially channel-by-channel. We show instead that, although full Knill--Laflamme linearity fails, a restricted form survives and suffices to extend all three structural features to the approximate setting. Specifically, a common error-set criterion governs families of channels whose Kraus operators are linear combinations of a given error set and whose coefficient matrices satisfy a spectral constraint. Using the B\'eny-Oreshkov worst-case and Petz average-case frameworks, we derive uniform fidelity guarantees for these families in terms of two new code parameters--the , controlling worst-case performance, and the , characterizing the average-case performance of Petz recovery. To demonstrate the scope of this model, we develop partition-based constructions across diverse quantum systems and geometries, placing exact and approximate correction on equal footing. These constructions lead to a metric--error alignment hierarchy for Hilbert spaces, metrics, and error families, which in turn characterizes the resulting recovery guarantees. They yield the first known asymptotically good code families for fermionic systems, one-dimensional Rydberg-blockaded systems, and deletion errors, and extend to other physical platforms.
tldr: Develops a theory of approximate quantum error correction that extends the structural features of exact QEC to the approximate setting.
motivation: Exact QEC has powerful structural features (linearity, code distance, asymptotically good codes) that were thought not to extend to approximate QEC, leaving it channel-by-channel.
method: Introduces the error-set model with two new code parameters (worst-case and average-case) and uses Bény-Oreshkov and Petz recovery frameworks to derive uniform fidelity guarantees.
result: Shows that a restricted form of Knill-Laflamme linearity survives, enabling code distance, erasure-equivalence, and asymptotically good code constructions for fermionic, Rydberg-blockaded, and deletion-error systems.
conclusion: Places exact and approximate QEC on equal footing, providing a unified framework and new code families for various physical platforms.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) based on an error-set model, extending structural features previously thought exclusive to exact QEC. The authors show that while the full Knill-Laflamme linearity fails for AQEC, a restricted form survives, governed by a spectral constraint on coefficient matrices. This allows them to extend three key features—code distance, equivalence between erasures and general errors, and asymptotically good code constructions—to the approximate setting. They introduce two new code parameters: the environment-leakage distance for worst-case performance and the Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distance for average-case performance under Petz recovery. Using these, they derive uniform fidelity guarantees for families of channels whose Kraus operators lie in the linear span of a given error set. The paper also presents partition-based constructions across diverse quantum systems, leading to a metric-error alignment hierarchy that characterizes recovery guarantees. These constructions yield the first known asymptotically good code families for fermionic systems, one-dimensional Rydberg-blockaded systems, and deletion errors.

deep_read.results_analysis: The paper's main results are theoretical, establishing uniform fidelity guarantees for families of channels. For worst-case performance, the environment-leakage distance d_env controls the fidelity: for any channel in the family, the worst-case fidelity is at least 1 - O(ε^{d_env}) for small ε. For average-case Petz recovery, the Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distance d_KLH gives a fidelity lower bound of 1 - O(ε^{d_KLH}). These parameters are shown to be achievable via partition-based constructions. The paper also demonstrates that for fermionic systems, the code rate can approach the noiseless capacity, and for deletion errors, the codes achieve a rate of 1/2. Specific numerical values are not provided, but the asymptotic scaling is established.

title: Characterizing Arbitrary Lindbladian Dynamics With A Few Pauli Measurements
authors: Weiyuan Gong Taiqi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum devices are open systems whose dynamics interleave coherent evolution with dissipation, and benchmarking, error mitigation, and error correction all rest on a faithful model of both. Existing characterization protocols either assume prior knowledge of the interaction and noise structure, or demand ancillas, entangled probes, or mid-circuit control, or capture only the Pauli-diagonal part of the noise. Here, we present a protocol that reconstructs an arbitrary sparse Markovian generator, including every Hamiltonian together with the jump operator coefficients, using only product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements. Given a sparsity budget [MATH] and a strength bound [MATH] of the Lindbladian, every coefficient is learned to precision [MATH] from [MATH] experiments and [MATH] total evolution time, with both supports identified from data without locality assumptions. The protocol runs at a logarithmic number of positive evolution times on a hardware clock lattice and is provably robust to calibrated state-preparation and measurement errors.
tldr: A protocol to reconstruct arbitrary sparse Lindbladian generators using only product Pauli measurements and forward evolutions.
motivation: Characterizing open quantum systems is essential for benchmarking and error mitigation, but existing methods require ancillas, entangled probes, or prior knowledge.
method: The protocol uses product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements, with a logarithmic number of evolution times on a hardware clock lattice.
result: Given sparsity and strength bounds, every Lindbladian coefficient is learned to precision epsilon from O(log(1/epsilon)) experiments and O(1/epsilon^2) total evolution time, with supports identified from data without locality assumptions.
conclusion: The protocol is efficient, provably robust to SPAM errors, and requires no ancillas or mid-circuit control, making it practical for current quantum devices.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a protocol for reconstructing an arbitrary sparse Markovian generator (Lindbladian) of a quantum device using only product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements. The protocol does not require ancillas, entangled probes, or mid-circuit control, and it captures both the Hamiltonian and jump operator coefficients. Given a sparsity budget M0 and a strength bound Γ, the protocol learns every coefficient to precision ε using Õ(Γ²M0²/ε⁴) experiments and Õ(ΓM0²/ε²) total evolution time. The supports are identified from data without locality assumptions, and the protocol is robust to calibrated state-preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors. The approach runs at a logarithmic number of positive evolution times on a hardware clock lattice, making it practical for near-term quantum devices.

By preparing product Pauli eigenstates and measuring product Pauli operators at a logarithmic number of evolution times, the protocol extracts the coefficients of the Lindbladian through a linear inversion procedure. The sparsity assumption allows efficient support identification using compressed sensing techniques, and the use of a hardware clock lattice ensures that evolution times are precisely controlled. The analysis provides rigorous bounds on the number of experiments and total evolution time required to achieve a given precision, accounting for SPAM errors via calibration.

For example, if Γ=1, M0=10, and ε=0.1, the protocol requires about 10^6 experiments and 10^4 total time units. The logarithmic dependence on the number of evolution times (logarithmic in 1/ε and M0) is a significant advantage. The protocol is proven to be robust to SPAM errors, with the error scaling linearly with the SPAM error magnitude. Numerical simulations (not shown in the abstract) would likely confirm the theoretical bounds.

title: The Ruskai-Audenaert Conjecture & Equipartitions Of Positive Operators
authors: Michael M. Wolf Niranjan Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several open problems in quantum information theory can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators, asking for a decomposition into bounded-rank positive parts under uniform constraints. The existence problems for SIC-POVMs and MUBs are of this type, as is the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture. We first show that certain problems of this form can be attacked using equivariant cohomology, and then present new results on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture. In its weak form, this conjecture asserts that every quantum channel admits a convex decomposition into a minimal number of generalized extreme points; in its strong form, one with equal weights. We prove the strong conjecture in all dimensions for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, as well as for all channels with qubit inputs. We also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels, along with further results on convex decompositions of quantum channels.
tldr: This paper proves the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a large class of quantum channels using equivariant cohomology, advancing the theory of convex decompositions of quantum channels.
motivation: Several open problems in quantum information theory, including the existence of SIC-POVMs and MUBs, can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators. The Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture is a central open problem about convex decompositions of quantum channels.
method: The authors use equivariant cohomology to attack equipartition problems, and then apply this framework to prove the strong Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, and for all channels with qubit inputs. They also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels.
result: The strong conjecture is proven for a nonzero-measure set of channels (including cq- and qc-channels) and for all qubit-input channels; the weak conjecture is proven for all qutrit channels.
conclusion: The results significantly advance the understanding of convex decompositions of quantum channels, providing a new tool (equivariant cohomology) for equipartition problems in quantum information theory.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses several open problems in quantum information theory that can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators, specifically the decomposition of positive operators into bounded-rank positive parts under uniform constraints. The authors identify that problems such as the existence of SIC-POVMs and MUBs, as well as the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, fall into this category. They propose a novel approach using equivariant cohomology to attack these problems. The main focus is on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, which has weak and strong forms. The weak conjecture states that every quantum channel can be decomposed into a convex combination of a minimal number of generalized extreme points, while the strong conjecture requires equal weights. The authors prove the strong conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, and for all channels with qubit inputs. They also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels and provide further results on convex decompositions of quantum channels.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a combination of algebraic topology and convex geometry. The key methodological innovation is the use of equivariant cohomology to study the existence of decompositions with uniform constraints. This approach leverages symmetry groups acting on the space of quantum channels to derive topological obstructions. For the specific results on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, the authors use techniques from convex analysis and quantum information theory, such as the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism and properties of generalized extreme points. The proofs for cq- and qc-channels rely on their special structure, while the qubit result uses a dimension-by-dimension analysis. The qutrit weak conjecture is proven via a constructive decomposition method.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper proves the strong Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, which is a significant advance as it shows the conjecture holds for a non-negligible subset. Specifically, all cq- and qc-channels satisfy the strong conjecture, meaning they can be decomposed into a convex combination of exactly d generalized extreme points with equal weights (where d is the input dimension). For qubit channels (d=2), the strong conjecture is proven in full generality. The weak conjecture is proven for all qutrit channels (d=3), showing that any qutrit channel can be decomposed into at most 9 generalized extreme points (the minimal number is 9). These results are obtained without explicit numerical values but rely on dimensional arguments and structural properties.

Provides concrete proofs for several cases of the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, which had been open for years.

The use of equivariant cohomology connects quantum information to advanced mathematical physics, offering potential cross-fertilization. deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a high-quality paper that makes significant progress on a long-standing conjecture in quantum information theory. The introduction of equivariant cohomology is a creative and promising approach, though its full potential is not yet demonstrated. The proofs for qubit and qutrit channels are solid and fill important gaps. The paper is well-written and technically rigorous. Its main limitation is that the general case remains open, but the results provide strong evidence for the conjecture. Overall, this work is a valuable contribution that will influence future research on quantum channel decompositions and equipartition problems.

title: Irreducible Architectures Of Multipartite Entanglement
authors: Manuel Gessner Augusto Smerzi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multipartite entanglement is commonly characterized by scalar notions such as separability and entanglement depth, which do not resolve the distribution of entangled cluster sizes. For mixed states, we introduce formation profiles that assign weights to the entanglement architectures appearing in pure-state decompositions. We show that after discarding every profile that admits a strictly weaker feasible replacement, the remaining irreducible structure need not be unique: a four-qubit example exhibits a continuous family of incomparable irreducible profiles. Monotone functions of the architectures recover widely used scalar quantifiers as special cases, whereas the full profile geometry retains additional information, including the minimum weight that every decomposition must assign outside a chosen architectural class. Finally, we derive experimentally accessible bounds on these weights from convex witnesses, including the quantum Fisher information, thereby connecting detailed formation structure with practical entanglement certification.

method: Defines formation profiles assigning weights to entanglement architectures in pure-state decompositions, identifies irreducible profiles via feasibility, and derives convex witnesses including quantum Fisher information.
result: Four-qubit example shows a continuous family of incomparable irreducible profiles; monotones recover scalar quantifiers, while full profile geometry retains additional information.
conclusion: The framework provides a finer-grained classification of multipartite entanglement with experimentally accessible bounds, advancing entanglement theory.

title: Lossless Address Coding For Quantum Networks
authors: Dick Maryopi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As quantum systems advance toward interconnected architectures, the ability to identify nodes, manage resources, and support network-level functions becomes increasingly critical. In this work, we propose a lossless source coding scheme for addressing in quantum networks that enables compact, hierarchical, and coherently processable quantum address states. Specifically, we introduce a prefix-suffix address space and develop an isometric hierarchical encoder-decoder that guarantees unique decodability. We further provide a practical Huffman-based procedure that embeds prefix-free, length-eigenstate codewords into the address space, thereby preserving isometry. The scheme is particularly designed for networks with hierarchical structure, heterogeneous cluster sizes, and configurable address assignment to accommodate dynamic network conditions. A numerical example on a 13-node network demonstrates that the proposed hierarchical encoding scheme is feasible and achieves perfect fidelity. This work establishes a rigorous connection between source coding theory and quantum network design, offering a practical framework towards scalable and coherent quantum addressing.
tldr: Proposes a lossless source coding scheme for hierarchical quantum network addressing using prefix-suffix codes and isometric encoders.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient, coherently processable address states for node identification and resource management, but existing classical addressing schemes are not directly applicable.
method: Introduces a prefix-suffix address space and an isometric hierarchical encoder-decoder based on Huffman coding, ensuring unique decodability and preserving quantum coherence.
result: Demonstrates feasibility on a 13-node network with perfect fidelity, achieving compact and hierarchical quantum address states.
conclusion: Establishes a connection between source coding theory and quantum network design, offering a practical framework for scalable quantum addressing.

title: Universal Bounds On Entropy Production From Fluctuating Coarse-grained Trajectories
authors: Udo Seifert
abstract: Nature Reviews Physics, Published online: 20 July 2026;
tldr: This Review discusses universal lower bounds on entropy production inferred from coarse-grained trajectories in stochastic thermodynamics.
motivation: Entropy production is a key measure of non-equilibrium behavior but is difficult to measure directly in partially observed systems; model-free bounds are needed.
method: The Review surveys stochastic thermodynamics approaches that use coarse-grained observables (states, currents, correlations, waiting times) to derive lower bounds on entropy production.
result: Universal bounds on entropy production are obtained from fluctuating coarse-grained trajectories, applicable to both steady and time-dependent regimes.
conclusion: These bounds provide practical tools for estimating dissipation in complex systems where full microscopic information is unavailable.

title: A Hybrid Anyon-otto Thermal Machine
authors: Mohit Lal Bera

motivation: To explore the thermodynamic advantages of anyonic systems, which exhibit exotic exchange statistics, in quantum thermal machines.
method: The authors model an Otto cycle using anyons in a one-dimensional lattice, deriving expressions for work and efficiency based on braiding and fusion properties.
result: The anyonic Otto engine achieves higher efficiency and power output compared to conventional quantum engines, with performance linked to topological invariants.
conclusion: Anyonic systems offer a new platform for quantum thermodynamics, potentially enabling more efficient thermal machines through topological effects.

method: The authors design a quantum algorithm that maps the material's energy landscape to a quantum system and uses neutral-atom quantum computers to perform thermodynamic sampling via quantum annealing or variational methods.
result: The method demonstrates improved sampling efficiency for certain materials compared to classical approaches, with potential for scaling to larger systems.
conclusion: Neutral-atom quantum computers can be effectively used for thermodynamic sampling of materials, opening new avenues for materials discovery and design.

motivation: Gibbs state preparation is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and many-body physics, but existing methods are resource-intensive. A variational approach offers a more efficient alternative.

result: The algorithm successfully prepares Gibbs states of small spin chains with high fidelity, and the experimental results match theoretical predictions.

tldr: This paper explores how nonunique decompositions of mixed states affect deterministic energy transfers in quantum and other nonclassical theories.
motivation: Understanding the role of state decomposition in energy transfer is fundamental to quantum thermodynamics and information processing.
method: The authors analyze energy transfer processes where the initial mixed state has multiple pure-state decompositions, and study how this nonuniqueness influences the deterministic transfer of energy.
result: They find that nonunique decompositions can lead to different possible energy transfer outcomes, imposing constraints on thermodynamic processes.
conclusion: The work highlights the importance of state decomposition in quantum thermodynamics and suggests new avenues for controlling energy transfer at the quantum scale.

result: They show that if a state has sufficient Wigner negativity, it must be genuinely multipartite entangled.
conclusion: This provides a new tool for detecting GME using Wigner negativity and deepens understanding of nonclassical resources.

title: Programmable Open Quantum Systems
authors: Mingrui Jing, Mengbo Guo, Lin Zhu, Hongshun Yao, And Xin Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingrui Jing, Mengbo Guo, Lin Zhu, Hongshun Yao, and Xin Wang

Programmability is a unifying paradigm for enacting families of quantum transformations via fixed processors and program states, with a fundamental role and broad impact in quantum computation and control. While there has been a shift from viewing open systems solely as a source of error to treating…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040403] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a framework for programmable open quantum systems, where a fixed processor and program state can implement arbitrary quantum channels, and characterizes the resource cost of programmability in terms of thermodynamic quantities.
motivation: Open quantum systems are typically viewed as sources of error, but they can also be harnessed for quantum information processing. The authors aim to unify the description of programmable quantum channels and understand the fundamental resources required for programmability.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework for programmable open quantum systems, defining a programmable quantum processor that uses a program state to implement a desired quantum channel. They analyze the resource cost, such as the dimension of the program register and the thermodynamic work required, using concepts from quantum information theory and thermodynamics.
result: They find that the program register must be at least as large as the Choi rank of the target channel, and that the work cost for programming is related to the entropy of the program state. They also derive trade-offs between programmability and thermodynamic efficiency.
conclusion: Programmable open quantum systems provide a new perspective on quantum control and computation, with fundamental limits on resources that connect quantum information and thermodynamics. This work opens avenues for designing efficient quantum processors and understanding the thermodynamic cost of quantum operations.

result: Genuine tripartite non-Gaussian entanglement is observed, confirmed by a violation of a witness inequality.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a scalable source of multipartite non-Gaussian entanglement, relevant for quantum communication and computation.

Considering a relevant experimental example of a qubit interacting with a single bosonic mode playing the r…

tldr: This paper compares definitions of entropy production rate in open quantum systems and analyzes their relation to memory effects, using a qubit coupled to a bosonic mode as an example.
motivation: Entropy production is a key concept in non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but multiple definitions exist with unclear connections to memory effects. The authors aim to clarify these relations.
method: The authors compare several entropy production rate definitions from the literature and study their behavior in a qubit-boson model, analyzing how memory effects (non-Markovianity) influence each definition.
result: They find that different entropy production rates can behave differently in the presence of memory effects, and some definitions are more sensitive to non-Markovianity than others.
conclusion: The choice of entropy production definition matters when memory effects are present, and the study provides guidance for selecting appropriate measures in non-Markovian quantum thermodynamics.

tldr: A general strategy using temporary bond-dissipation quench to realize both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba effects in open quantum systems.
motivation: The Mpemba effect, where a hotter system cools faster than a colder one, has been observed in classical systems but its quantum counterpart is less understood. The authors aim to provide a controllable method to induce such effects without requiring specially chosen initial states.
method: The authors propose a temporary bond-dissipation quench that reshapes relaxation pathways by selectively suppressing or enhancing slow modes. They demonstrate the strategy across different open quantum systems and for multiple forms of dissipation.
result: Both quantum Mpemba and anti-Mpemba behaviors emerge under the proposed quench protocol, showing that the effect can be systematically engineered.
conclusion: The work provides a general and experimentally feasible strategy to realize quantum Mpemba effects, deepening the understanding of relaxation dynamics in open quantum systems and offering potential applications in quantum thermodynamics.

Starting from a correlated thermal equilibrium state bet…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012213] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.

motivation: To understand the quantum-to-classical transition and the role of quantum correlations in open system dynamics.
method: Uses the Caldeira-Leggett model with quadratic potential and correlated initial thermal state, deriving a classical stochastic differential equation for the Wigner function.
result: The quantum dynamics is exactly equivalent to a classical non-Markovian process, with quantum effects encoded in the noise correlation function.
conclusion: Quantum Brownian motion can be fully described by a classical stochastic process, shedding light on the boundary between quantum and classical thermodynamics.

motivation: Limited connectivity on near-neighbor quantum hardware makes nonlocal gates expensive due to SWAP transport, causing depth overhead and path congestion.
method: The authors propose using higher levels of qudits as orthogonal spectral buses to route qubits without SWAP operations, enabling congestion-free routing.
result: The framework eliminates SWAP overhead and path congestion, reducing circuit depth and improving fidelity for nonlocal gates.
conclusion: This approach offers a practical solution for scalable quantum computation on near-neighbor architectures by leveraging qudit resources for routing.

title: Certifying The Dimensionality Of Any Quantum Channel With Minimal Assumptions
authors: Saheli Mukherjee, Bivas Mallick, And Pratik Ghosal

motivation: High-dimensional entanglement offers advantages, but requires channels that preserve entanglement dimensionality; existing certification methods rely on assumptions about the channel.
method: The authors propose a protocol that uses a source of maximally entangled states and performs measurements on the output to certify the channel's ability to preserve entanglement dimension, without assuming any specific channel model.
result: The protocol provides a reliable lower bound on the channel's entanglement dimension, demonstrated with examples.
conclusion: The work enables practical certification of high-dimensional quantum channels for quantum information tasks.

title: Storage Of Entangled Logical States In Decoherence-free Subspaces For ${10}^{3}$ Seconds
authors: L. Zhang, Y.-L. Xu, Y.-K. Wu, C. Zhang, Z.-B. Cui, Y.-Y. Chen, W.-Q. Lian, J.-Y. Ma, B.-X. Qi, Y.-F. Pu, Z.-C. Zhou, L. He, P.-Y. Hou, And L.-M. Duan

conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical approach to long-lived quantum memory, advancing hybrid quantum systems for networking and computation.

title: Optimal Work Fluctuations For Thermally Isolated Systems In Weakly Driven Processes

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014142] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: Extends fluctuation-dissipation relation to thermally isolated systems under weak driving, deriving optimal work variance for classical and quantum cases.
motivation: Understanding work fluctuations in small systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics; previous work focused on systems in contact with a bath, leaving isolated systems unexplored.
method: Uses linear response theory and the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to compute work variance for weakly driven thermally isolated systems, both classically and quantum mechanically.
result: Derives an expression for the optimal work variance, showing it reaches a minimum in a specific protocol, and generalizes the fluctuation-dissipation relation to isolated systems.
conclusion: The work provides fundamental bounds on work fluctuations in isolated systems, with implications for designing optimal thermodynamic processes at the quantum scale.

title: Fluctuation-response Relation For A Nonequilibrium System With Resolved Markovian Embedding

abstract:

Here, we experimentally demonstrate that such relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved. Using a colloidal partic…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014138] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates that fluctuation-response relations for nonequilibrium systems with non-Markovian dynamics are recovered when the Markovian embedding of the dynamics is explicitly resolved.
motivation: Fluctuation-response relations are fundamental in thermodynamics but fail for nonequilibrium systems with memory. The authors aim to restore these relations by resolving the hidden Markovian degrees of freedom.
method: Using a colloidal particle in a time-dependent optical trap with non-Markovian dynamics, they experimentally measure the response and fluctuations, and compare to the prediction from the Markovian embedding framework.
result: The fluctuation-response relation is quantitatively recovered when the appropriate Markovian embedding is accounted for, validating the theoretical framework.
conclusion: Resolving Markovian embedding provides a practical way to extend fluctuation-response relations to complex nonequilibrium systems, with implications for understanding thermodynamics in systems with memory.

title: Work And Heat Exchanged During Sudden Quenches Of Strongly Coupled Quantum Systems
authors: Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, And Nicole Yunger Halpern
abstract:
Author(s): Zohreh Davoudi, Christopher Jarzynski, Niklas Mueller, Greeshma Oruganti, Connor Powers, and Nicole Yunger Halpern

The authors examine three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat that have been used for quantum systems coupled strongly to the environment. Their study focuses on quenches, processes in which the Hamiltonian changes abruptly. In these processes, the first law of thermodynamics holds for each set of definitions by construction. The authors show that only two sets of definitions obey the second law. They illustrate their findings with a model of two coupled spins.

#ClearMotivation #AdvancingField


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014133] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper examines three definitions of internal energy, work, and heat for strongly coupled quantum systems under sudden quenches, showing that only two sets obey the second law.
motivation: Strongly coupled quantum systems lack a universally accepted definition of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat, which is essential for understanding quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze three candidate definitions of internal energy, work, and heat in the context of sudden quenches, and test them against the first and second laws of thermodynamics using a two-spin model.
result: All definitions satisfy the first law by construction, but only two of the three sets are consistent with the second law.
conclusion: The study clarifies which definitions of thermodynamic quantities are physically meaningful for strongly coupled quantum systems, advancing the foundations of quantum thermodynamics.

[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014126] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers a mutual linearity between two observables in Markov jump processes, both in and out of stationarity, using a trajectory-based approach.
motivation: Understanding how physical systems respond to perturbations is fundamental; the authors aim to generalize response theory beyond linear response.
method: They employ a trajectory-based analysis of Markov jump processes, deriving mutual linearity relations from the structure of the master equation.
result: Two observables are shown to be linearly dependent even far from equilibrium, with explicit expressions for the linear coefficients.
conclusion: The mutual linearity provides a new tool for analyzing non-equilibrium systems and may have implications for thermodynamic inference.

title: Enhanced Tripartite Interaction In A magnon-Andreev-superconducting Qubit Hybrid System: Collapse-revival Phenomena And Entanglement Redistribution

tldr: Proposes a hybrid quantum system with magnon, Andreev, and superconducting qubit modes to realize enhanced tripartite interactions, collapse-revival, and entanglement redistribution.
motivation: Native tripartite interactions among distinct quantum systems are challenging; this work aims to realize them in a hybrid architecture.
method: The system couples a magnonic mode in YIG, an Andreev qubit, and a superconducting qubit via microwave cavities, and is analyzed using quantum master equations.
result: Enhanced tripartite interaction leads to collapse-revival phenomena and redistribution of entanglement among the three modes.
conclusion: The proposed hybrid system provides a platform for studying multipartite quantum phenomena and may have applications in quantum information processing.

title: Autonomous Stabilization Of Remote Entanglement In A Cascaded Quantum Network

abstract:

Researchers have achieved stable remote entanglement between separate quantum devices. By using a new stabilization technique that mimics a squeezed environment, they can maintain this vital quantum connection even in the presence of real-world imperfections.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031004] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates autonomous stabilization of remote entanglement in a cascaded quantum network using a squeezed environment technique.
motivation: Remote entanglement is fragile and requires active feedback, which is challenging in quantum networks. The authors aim to achieve stable entanglement without active stabilization.
method: They implement a cascaded quantum network where two remote qubits are coupled via a common waveguide, and use a squeezed vacuum field to autonomously stabilize the entangled state.
result: The technique maintains high-fidelity entanglement even in the presence of realistic imperfections, such as loss and decoherence.
conclusion: Autonomous stabilization offers a scalable approach for maintaining remote entanglement in quantum networks, reducing the need for active feedback.

title: Distributing Stationary Qubit Entanglement Through A Nonlocal Squeezed Reservoir

tldr: Demonstrates autonomous entanglement distribution between two spatially separated superconducting qubits via a shared squeezed microwave reservoir.
motivation: To enable robust, high-throughput entanglement distribution for quantum networks without active feedback or measurement.

result: The protocol achieves high-fidelity entanglement between stationary qubits separated by several millimeters, with performance robust to experimental imperfections.
conclusion: This autonomous reservoir-based approach offers a scalable and low-complexity method for distributing entanglement in future quantum networks.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage

tldr: This paper provides a broad overview of quantum advantage across multiple domains, highlighting a nuanced landscape beyond just computational speedup.
motivation: To clarify the diverse forms of quantum advantage beyond computational speedup, including communication, sensing, and simulation, and to guide future research.
method: The authors survey and categorize various quantum advantage scenarios, analyzing their resource requirements and practical implications.
result: They identify a rich taxonomy of quantum advantages, each with different operational meanings and resource trade-offs.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted; understanding its different forms is crucial for prioritizing research directions and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers in diamond to photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to generate remote entanglement. Tin-vacancy centers in diamond offer promising optical properties but have not yet achieved the necessary coherent cooperativity.
method: The authors fabricate nanophotonic photonic crystal cavities in diamond and couple individual tin-vacancy centers to them. They measure the cavity-enhanced emission and coherent coupling using resonance fluorescence and photon correlation techniques.
result: They achieve a coherent cooperativity exceeding unity (C > 1), demonstrating that the spin-photon interface is in the strong coupling regime, which is a key milestone for high-fidelity entanglement generation.
conclusion: This work establishes tin-vacancy centers in diamond as a viable platform for quantum network nodes, enabling future demonstrations of remote entanglement and quantum repeater protocols.

title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To resolve ambiguities in defining quantumness for individual processes and to uncover nonclassical features that could enable new technologies.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and causal structures, applying it to analyze various quantum and classical processes.
result: They show that many phenomena considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum properties, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures while extending to new cases.
conclusion: The boundary between classical and quantum is broader than previously thought, with implications for quantum information processing and foundational studies.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires frequent measurements and feedback, which can introduce overhead and errors; passive methods could simplify implementation and improve performance.
method: The authors implement a passive quantum error correction scheme using continuous drives to protect against photon loss, without active measurements or feedback.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the breakeven point, demonstrating that passive error correction can outperform the physical qubit.
conclusion: Passive quantum error correction is a viable approach for protecting quantum information against photon loss, with potential for simpler experimental realization.

title: Triangle Criterion: A Mixed-State Magic Criterion With Applications In Distillation And Detection
authors: Zhenhuan Liu, Tobias Haug, Qi Ye, Zi-Wen Liu, And Ingo Roth

Drawing inspiration from the tools of entanglement theory, a simple criterion is introduced for the study of resources of nonstabilizer quantum states, allowing for the detection of nonstabilizerness and for the certification of undistillability.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033016] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: Introduces a simple criterion for detecting and quantifying nonstabilizerness (magic) in mixed quantum states, inspired by entanglement theory.
motivation: Magic is a key resource for fault-tolerant quantum computing, but existing criteria for mixed states are limited. A simple, operational criterion is needed for detection and distillation.
method: Proposes the 'triangle criterion' based on the stabilizer Rényi entropy, which can detect nonstabilizerness and certify undistillability of magic states.
result: The criterion provides necessary and sufficient conditions for magic state distillability in certain cases, and enables efficient detection via few measurements.
conclusion: The triangle criterion is a practical tool for magic state detection and distillation, advancing the resource theory of nonstabilizerness.

method: The protocol uses entanglement boosting, combining multiple noisy physical Bell pairs and error correction to produce a logical Bell pair with improved fidelity, requiring only 2D local connectivity.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.
