A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in cavity QED systems with long-range interactions and kinetic constraints.
method: Theoretical analysis of a cavity-coupled Rydberg array model with kinetic constraints, using analytical and numerical methods to study steady-state phases and dynamics.
result: Discovery of blockaded ferromagnetism and long-range quantum scars as emergent phenomena from the interplay of cavity-mediated interactions and kinetic constraints.
conclusion: Cavity QED with kinetic constraints provides a platform for realizing novel quantum many-body phases, relevant for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions for enhanced parameter estimation, surpassing classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, offering a resource for high-precision sensing beyond classical bounds.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including scaling analysis and Fisher information.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum systems can achieve Heisenberg-limited sensitivity, with examples from various physical platforms.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing provides a robust and practical route to ultra-precise measurements, with potential applications in quantum metrology.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: To achieve high-fidelity quantum control in non-adiabatic regimes, counterdiabatic driving is effective but often requires complex auxiliary Hamiltonians; this work aims to simplify and improve the variational approach.
method: The authors introduce a weighted action functional and employ computer algebra to systematically derive optimal variational counterdiabatic Hamiltonians.
result: The new method yields significantly higher fidelity compared to standard variational counterdiabatic driving in several test systems.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and readily implementable upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and quantum information processing.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory with emphasis on symmetry, topology, and purity.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The authors employ nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior in driven open many-body systems, focusing on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: They identify distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking them to symmetry and topological features.
conclusion: The review provides a systematic classification of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, offering a foundation for understanding nonequilibrium stationary states.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, given that classical gravity with quantum matter may be inconsistent; information-theoretic methods provide model-independent constraints.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks using quantum information concepts (e.g., entanglement, channel capacity) to design tabletop experiments that detect gravitationally induced entanglement between two quantum probes.
result: Several proposed experiments are analyzed, showing that gravitationally induced entanglement can be used to test the quantum nature of gravity, with potential feasibility in the near future.
conclusion: Quantum information methods offer a promising path to experimentally probe quantum gravity, with tabletop experiments potentially resolving foundational questions about the nature of gravity.

title: Quantum Nonlocality Without Entanglement And State Discrimination Measures
authors: Shayeef Murshid, Tathagata Gupta, Vincent Russo, And Somshubhro Bandyopadhyay
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2174 (2026).

An ensemble of product states is said to exhibit “quantum nonlocality without entanglement” if it cannot be optimally discriminated using local operations and classical communication (LOCC). We show that this property can depend on the chosen discrimination measure. Specifically, we construct a family of ensembles, each consisting of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states, for which LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds in achieving optimal unambiguous discrimination. We further extend our construction to multipartite systems and provide strong numerical evidence that a similar separation between local and global optima is present for minimum-error discrimination, but not for unambiguous discrimination.

.
tldr: This paper shows that quantum nonlocality without entanglement can depend on the discrimination measure, with LOCC achieving optimal unambiguous but not minimum-error discrimination for certain product-state ensembles.
motivation: To understand whether the phenomenon of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is robust under different operational tasks (minimum-error vs. unambiguous discrimination).
method: Constructs explicit families of six linearly independent, equally probable bipartite product states and analyzes their optimal discrimination under LOCC for both minimum-error and unambiguous discrimination measures; extends to multipartite systems with numerical evidence.
result: LOCC fails to achieve optimal minimum-error discrimination but succeeds for unambiguous discrimination for the constructed ensembles, showing a separation between the two measures.
conclusion: The property of quantum nonlocality without entanglement is not absolute but depends on the chosen discrimination measure, highlighting the nuanced role of LOCC constraints in state discrimination.

title: Non-commutative Optimization Problems With Differential Constraints
authors: Mateus Araújo, Andrew J. P. Garner, And Miguel Navascués
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2169 (2026).

Non-commutative polynomial optimization (NPO) problems seek to minimize the state average of a polynomial of some operator variables, subject to polynomial constraints, over all states and operators, as well as the Hilbert spaces where those might be defined. Many of these problems are known to admit a complete hierarchy of semidefinite programming (SDP) relaxations. In this work, we consider a variant of NPO problems where a subset of the operator variables satisfies a system of ordinary differential equations. We prove that, under mild conditions of operator boundedness, for every such problem one can construct a standard NPO problem with the same solution. This allows us to define a complete hierarchy of SDPs to tackle the original differential problem. We apply this method to bound averages of local observables in quantum spin systems subject to a Hamiltonian evolution (i.e., a quench). We find that, even in the thermodynamic limit of infinitely many sites, low levels of the hierarchy provide very good approximations for reasonably long evolution times.

.
tldr: Extends non-commutative polynomial optimization to problems with differential constraints, enabling SDP relaxations for quantum spin systems under Hamiltonian evolution.
motivation: Many quantum optimization problems involve time-dependent constraints, but standard NPO cannot handle differential equations. This work bridges that gap.
method: Proves that under boundedness conditions, differential NPO problems can be reformulated as standard NPO problems, then applies a known SDP hierarchy.
result: The method yields tight bounds on local observables in quantum spin systems even in the thermodynamic limit and for long evolution times.
conclusion: Provides a practical tool for analyzing quantum dynamics via convex optimization, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Resource Quantification For Programming Low-depth Quantum Circuits
authors: Entong He And Yuxiang Yang
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2166 (2026).

Noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices pave the way for implementing quantum algorithms that offer quantum advantages over their classical counterparts. Due to the intrinsic noise and decoherence in the physical system, NISQ machines are naturally modeled as large-scale, low-depth quantum circuits. In practice, executing such circuits requires sending program states that encode the relevant instructions to a programmable quantum computer, typically through a cloud service. Existing programming approaches designed for generic unitary transformations are computationally inefficient in the low-depth setting, and therefore remain unsatisfactory. As such, to realize NISQ algorithms, it is crucial to find an efficient way to program low-depth circuits as the number of qubits [MATH] increases. Here, we investigate the circuit complexity and the size of quantum memory, known as the program cost, required to program low-depth brickwork circuits. We establish a tight worst-case program cost of [MATH] for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-[MATH] regime. Moreover, we analyze the trade-off between the cost of describing the layout of local gates and the cost of programming them to implement the target unitaries via the light-cone argument. Our findings suggest that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal in the low-depth regime.

.
tldr: This paper establishes tight worst-case program cost for programming low-depth brickwork circuits, showing that faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal.
motivation: Existing programming approaches for generic unitary transformations are inefficient for low-depth circuits needed in NISQ devices, so an efficient method to program such circuits is crucial.
method: The authors analyze circuit complexity and quantum memory size (program cost) required to program low-depth brickwork circuits, using a light-cone argument to trade off layout description cost and programming cost.
result: They prove a tight worst-case program cost of O(n log n) for universally programming low-depth brickwork circuits in the large-n regime.
conclusion: Faithful gate-wise programming is essentially optimal for low-depth circuits, providing a practical guideline for NISQ algorithm implementation.

title: Fast Quantum Measurement Tomography With Optimal Error Bounds
authors: Leonardo Zambrano, Sergi Ramos-Calderer, And Richard Kueng
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2162 (2026).

We present a two-step protocol for quantum measurement tomography that is light on classical co-processing cost and still achieves optimal sample complexity. Given measurement data from a known probe state ensemble, we first apply least-squares estimation to produce an unconstrained approximation of the POVM, and then project this estimate onto the set of valid quantum measurements. For a POVM with [MATH] outcomes acting on a [MATH]-dimensional system, we show that the protocol requires [MATH] samples to achieve error [MATH] in worst-case distance, and [MATH] samples in average-case distance. We further establish two matching sample complexity lower bounds of [MATH] and [MATH] for any non-adaptive, single-copy POVM tomography protocol. Hence, our projected least squares POVM tomography is sample-optimal in both the dimension and the number of outcomes for both distances. Our method admits an analytic form when using global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles and enables rigorous non-asymptotic error guarantees. Finally, we also complement our findings with empirical performance studies carried out on a noisy superconducting quantum computer with flux-tunable transmon qubits.

.
tldr: A sample-optimal quantum measurement tomography protocol using projected least squares estimation with rigorous error bounds.
motivation: Efficiently characterizing quantum measurements (POVMs) is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing tomography methods often require heavy classical post-processing or lack optimal sample complexity.
method: The protocol first applies least-squares estimation to measurement data from known probe states, then projects the unconstrained estimate onto the set of valid POVMs. It uses global or local 2-designs as probe ensembles.
result: The protocol achieves optimal sample complexity: O(d^2/ε^2) for worst-case distance and O(d/ε^2) for average-case distance, with matching lower bounds. It also provides non-asymptotic error guarantees.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, sample-optimal method for quantum measurement tomography with rigorous guarantees, advancing quantum characterization techniques.

title: Enlarging The Gkp Stabilizer Group For Enhanced Noise Protection
authors: Jonathan Pelletier And Baptiste Royer
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2156 (2026).

Encoding a qubit in a larger Hilbert space of an oscillator is an efficient way to protect its quantum information against decoherence. Promising examples of such bosonic encodings are the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) codes. In this work, we investigate how redefining the stabilizer group of the GKP codes to include all operations with trivial action on the code space can contribute to the search for an optimal implementation of a logical circuit when it is affected by noise. We find the generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group, allowing us to search for different physical implementations of a Clifford operation. We then propose an algorithm that finds the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, such that the state is less affected by loss errors during the computation. Finally, we demonstrate numerically, with logical randomized benchmarking, that such a compiler can increase the lifetime of square-GKP qubits while running Clifford circuits, compared to a random walk compiler.

.
tldr: This paper enlarges the GKP stabilizer group to include all operations with trivial action on the code space, enabling optimal implementation of Clifford circuits with enhanced noise protection.
motivation: GKP codes are promising for protecting quantum information in oscillators, but finding optimal physical implementations of logical circuits under noise remains challenging.
method: The authors identify generators of the Gaussian stabilizer group and propose an algorithm to find the optimal implementation of a given logical Clifford circuit on GKP codes, minimizing loss errors during computation.
result: Numerical simulations using logical randomized benchmarking show that the compiler increases the lifetime of square-GKP qubits running Clifford circuits compared to a random walk compiler.
conclusion: Redefining the stabilizer group to include all trivial-action operations provides a systematic way to enhance noise protection in GKP codes, with potential applications in fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Resourcefulness Of Non-classical Continuous-variable Quantum Gates
authors: Massimo Frigerio, Antoine Debray, Nicolas Treps, And Mattia Walschaers
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2155 (2026).

In continuous-variable quantum computation, identifying key elements that enable a quantum computational advantage is a long-standing issue. Starting from the standard results on the necessity of Wigner negativity, we develop a comprehensive and versatile approach in which the techniques of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobabilities are exploited to provide rigorous statements on the simulability of photonic quantum circuits consisting of previously characterized gates and thereby identifying the contribution of each quantum gate to the potential achievement of quantum computational advantage. This is achieved by means of an analysis of the so-called transfer function, allowing us to highlight the resourcefulness of a gate set. As such this technique can be straightforwardly applied to current continuous-variables quantum circuits, while also constraining the tolerable amount of losses above which any potential quantum advantage can be ruled out. We use [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space to capture the non-classical features in the protocol, and focus our technique entirely on the ordering parameter [MATH]. This allows us to highlight the resourcefulness and robustness to loss of a universal set of unitary gates comprising three distinct Gaussian gates and any non-Gaussian unitary gate, providing important insight on the role of non-Gaussianity.

.
tldr: Develops a comprehensive approach using s-ordered quasiprobabilities to quantify the resourcefulness of non-classical continuous-variable quantum gates for achieving quantum computational advantage.
motivation: Identifying key elements enabling quantum computational advantage in continuous-variable quantum computation is a long-standing issue; the paper aims to provide rigorous simulability criteria and resource quantification.
method: Exploits s-ordered quasiprobability distributions on phase-space and analyzes the transfer function of gate sets to characterize non-classical features and robustness to loss.
result: Provides a technique to highlight the resourcefulness of a universal set of unitary gates (three Gaussian plus any non-Gaussian) and constrains the tolerable loss above which quantum advantage is ruled out.
conclusion: The approach offers a versatile tool for assessing and comparing the non-classical resources of continuous-variable quantum circuits, with direct applicability to current experiments.

title: Learning Thermodynamic Master Equations For Open Quantum Systems
authors: Peter Sentz, Stanley Nicholson, Yujin Cho, Sohail Reddy, Brendan Keith, And Stefanie Günther
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2151 (2026).

The characterization of Hamiltonians and other components of open quantum dynamical systems plays a crucial role in quantum computing and other applications. Scientific machine learning techniques have been applied to this problem in a variety of ways, including by modeling with deep neural networks. However, the majority of mathematical models describing open quantum systems are linear, and the natural nonlinearities in learnable models have not been incorporated using physical principles. We present a data-driven model for open quantum systems that includes learnable, thermodynamically consistent terms. The trained model is interpretable, as it directly estimates the system Hamiltonian and linear components of coupling to the environment. We validate the model on synthetic two and three-level data, as well as experimental two-level data collected from a quantum device at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.

.
tldr: A data-driven model for open quantum systems that learns thermodynamically consistent Hamiltonians and coupling terms from measurement data.
motivation: Characterizing Hamiltonians and environmental couplings is crucial for quantum computing, but existing models often lack thermodynamic consistency or interpretability.
method: The authors propose a neural network model that incorporates physical principles to enforce thermodynamic consistency, directly estimating the system Hamiltonian and linear coupling terms.
result: The model is validated on synthetic two- and three-level systems and experimental two-level data from a quantum device, demonstrating accurate and interpretable recovery of system parameters.
conclusion: This work provides a practical, interpretable machine learning approach for modeling open quantum systems with built-in thermodynamic constraints, advancing quantum system identification.

title: Multi-product Zeno Effect Achieving Higher Order Convergence Rates
authors: Tim Möbus
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2148 (2026).

The quantum Zeno effect is a fundamental mechanism for implementing the effective dynamics of projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian systems. It approximates the target projected evolution by interleaving Hamiltonian or Lindblad dynamics with quantum operations associated with the desired subspace. In contrast to the related Trotter product formula, the best-known convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect is typically limited to order [MATH]. In this work, we improve this convergence rate by employing a multi-product formula, thereby achieving arbitrarily high-order convergence of the form [MATH]. This yields an improved approximation scheme for Zeno-like expectation values via an efficient post-processing method. The approach combines a modified Chernoff lemma, an adapted Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation. We illustrate the method with the bosonic cat code and also consider the broader class of systems governed by the Bang-Bang decoupling method.

.
tldr: This paper improves the convergence rate of the quantum Zeno effect to arbitrarily high order using a multi-product formula, with applications to projected Hamiltonian and Lindbladian dynamics.
motivation: The quantum Zeno effect typically has limited convergence rate; achieving higher-order convergence can improve approximation schemes for quantum dynamics.
method: The authors combine a modified Chernoff lemma, Dunford-Segal approximation, holomorphic functional calculus, and Chebyshev interpolation to construct a multi-product formula that yields higher-order convergence.
result: They demonstrate arbitrarily high-order convergence rates for the quantum Zeno effect, illustrated with the bosonic cat code and Bang-Bang decoupling.
conclusion: The multi-product Zeno effect provides a more efficient approximation for projected dynamics, with potential applications in quantum control and simulation.

title: On The Addressability Problem On Css Codes
authors: Jérôme Guyot And Samuel Jaques
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2145 (2026).

Recent discoveries in asymptotically good quantum codes have intensified research on their application in quantum computation and fault-tolerant operations. This study focuses on the addressability problem within CSS codes: we ask what circuits might implement logical gates on strict subsets of logical qubits. With some notion of fault-tolerance, we prove several impossibility results: for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address a logical [MATH], [MATH], [MATH], or [MATH] to any non-empty strict subset of logical qubits using a circuit made only from 1-local Clifford gates. Furthermore, we show that one cannot permute the logical qubits in a code purely by permuting the physical qubits, if the rate of the code is (asymptotically) greater than 1/3 and the distance is at least 3. We can show a similar no-go result for [MATH]s and [MATH]s between two such high-rate codes, albeit under a more restrictive assumption on the circuit, which we call "global" (though recent addressable CCZ gates use global circuits). This work pioneers the study of distance-preserving addressability in quantum codes, mainly by considering automorphisms of the code. This perspective offers new insights and potential directions for future research. We argue that studying this trade off between addressability and efficiency of the codes is essential to understand better how to do efficient quantum computation.

.
tldr: This paper proves impossibility results for addressing logical qubits in high-rate CSS codes using local Clifford circuits, and shows that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is limited by code rate.
motivation: Recent advances in asymptotically good quantum codes raise the question of how to implement logical gates on subsets of logical qubits, which is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
method: The authors use automorphism theory of CSS codes and combinatorial arguments to derive no-go theorems for addressability under various circuit constraints.
result: They prove that for CSS codes with non-zero rate, one cannot address logical X, Z, H, or S gates to a strict subset of logical qubits using 1-local Clifford circuits, and that permuting logical qubits via physical permutations is impossible if the rate exceeds 1/3 and distance is at least 3.
conclusion: The trade-off between addressability and code efficiency is fundamental, and this work provides new insights into the limitations of fault-tolerant operations on quantum codes.

title: Non-Abelian Geometric Phases In Triangular Structures And Universal Su(2) Control In Shape Space
authors: J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, And J. Westerholm
abstract:
Author(s): J. Dai, A. Molochkov, A. J. Niemi, and J. Westerholm

We construct holonomic quantum gates for qubits that are encoded in the near-degenerate vibrational [MATH] doublet of a deformable three-body system. Using Kendall's shape theory, we derive the Wilczek-Zee connection that governs adiabatic transport within the [MATH] manifold. We show that its restricted …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012212] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: The paper constructs holonomic quantum gates for qubits encoded in vibrational doublets of a three-body system using non-Abelian geometric phases.
motivation: To realize universal quantum gates via geometric phases that are robust against certain errors, leveraging the shape space of a deformable triangular molecule.
method: Using Kendall's shape theory to derive the Wilczek-Zee connection for adiabatic transport within a near-degenerate vibrational manifold, and showing that the holonomy yields SU(2) control.
result: The restricted Wilczek-Zee connection is an SU(2) gauge field, enabling universal single-qubit gates through cyclic deformations of the triangle.
conclusion: The triangular structure provides a platform for holonomic quantum computation with built-in geometric protection.

title: Characterizing high-Schmidt-number Witnesses In Arbitrary-dimensional Systems
authors: Liang Xiong And Nung-Sing Sze
abstract:
Author(s): Liang Xiong and Nung-sing Sze

A profound comprehension of quantum entanglement is crucial for the progression of quantum technologies. The degree of entanglement can be assessed by enumerating the entangled degrees of freedom, leading to the determination of a parameter known as the Schmidt number (SN). In this paper, we develop…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012443] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: Develops Schmidt number witnesses for arbitrary-dimensional systems, enabling experimental detection of high-dimensional entanglement.
motivation: Quantifying entanglement via Schmidt number is crucial for quantum technologies, but existing witnesses are limited to low dimensions.
method: Constructs linear witnesses based on expectation values of observables, optimized for detecting specific Schmidt numbers using semidefinite programming.
result: Provides explicit witnesses for arbitrary Schmidt numbers and dimensions, with improved noise tolerance compared to previous methods.
conclusion: The proposed witnesses are experimentally feasible and advance the characterization of high-dimensional entanglement.

title: Mixed State Entanglement Via The Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
authors: Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, And Chern Chuang
abstract:
Author(s): Nishaant Jacobus, Paul Brumer, and Chern Chuang

This work develops an approach to analyze the quantum entanglement of mixed states by comparing the relative magnitudes of populations and coherences of the density operator. This is applied to models of light-matter interaction to examine how the symmetries of the interaction influence entanglement in thermal and nonequilibrium steady states.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032014] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: Develops a method to analyze mixed-state entanglement using population-coherence comparison via Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, applied to light-matter interaction models.
motivation: Characterizing entanglement in mixed states is challenging; this work aims to provide a simpler approach based on density operator populations and coherences.
method: Uses the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality to relate populations and coherences, deriving a necessary condition for entanglement; applies to thermal and nonequilibrium steady states of light-matter systems.
result: The method reveals how interaction symmetries influence entanglement in mixed states, demonstrated on model systems.
conclusion: The population-coherence approach offers a practical tool for detecting mixed-state entanglement, particularly in open quantum systems.

title: Gravitational Acceleration Encoded In Jaynes Cummings Exchange Frequencies: Quantum Fisher Information, Readout, And Validity Conditions
authors: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Mohammad Haris Khan, Fardeen Ahmad Sofi, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an effective trapped atom--cavity model in which a constant gravitational acceleration shifts the oscillator equilibrium and changes the local standing-wave coupling, thereby encoding the acceleration in the Jaynes Cummings exchange frequencies. With the atom and motion initially in their ground states and the cavity field initially coherent, we solve the closed-system carrier dynamics exactly and derive the displaced-frame quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the joint atom-cavity state. This QFI is proportional to the square of the local coupling slope, grows quadratically with interrogation time, and scales linearly with mean photon number. At the node, phase-referenced Ramsey detection gives a sign-sensitive estimate of axial acceleration and locally saturates the joint QFI. Away from the node, photon counting and phase-optimized homodyne detection provide cavity readouts when the cavity state carries more QFI than the atomic state. At the off-node operating point studied, Lindblad simulations show that cavity loss produces a finite-time QFI optimum. Lamb Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions control the carrier approximation. In the closed-system benchmark, the carrier-model QFI agrees with the atom-cavity QFI obtained from the unexpanded model after tracing out motion.
tldr: A trapped atom-cavity system encodes gravitational acceleration in Jaynes-Cummings exchange frequencies, with quantum Fisher information analysis and readout schemes.
motivation: To develop a quantum sensor for gravitational acceleration using a hybrid atom-cavity platform, leveraging the sensitivity of Jaynes-Cummings dynamics.
method: Derives an effective model where gravity shifts the oscillator equilibrium and modifies the atom-cavity coupling; solves carrier dynamics exactly; computes quantum Fisher information for the joint state; and simulates cavity loss via Lindblad master equation.
result: The QFI scales quadratically with time and linearly with mean photon number; phase-referenced Ramsey detection at the node saturates the joint QFI; cavity loss creates a finite-time optimum.
conclusion: The proposed scheme can measure gravitational acceleration with high sensitivity, and the carrier approximation is valid under Lamb-Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper presents a theoretical framework for measuring gravitational acceleration using a trapped atom coupled to an optical cavity. The key idea is that gravity shifts the equilibrium position of the atom's motion and modifies the local coupling strength to the cavity field, encoding the acceleration in the Jaynes-Cummings exchange frequencies. The authors solve the closed-system dynamics exactly for an initially coherent cavity field and ground-state atom and motion, deriving the quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the joint state. They find that the QFI is proportional to the square of the local coupling slope, grows quadratically with interrogation time, and scales linearly with mean photon number. At the cavity node, phase-referenced Ramsey detection yields a sign-sensitive estimate of axial acceleration and locally saturates the joint QFI. Away from the node, photon counting and phase-optimized homodyne detection provide cavity readouts when the cavity state carries more QFI than the atomic state. Lindblad simulations including cavity loss show a finite-time QFI optimum at an off-node operating point. The paper also discusses the validity of the carrier approximation under Lamb-Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions.
key_contributions: Derivation of an effective trapped atom-cavity model where gravitational acceleration shifts the oscillator equilibrium and modifies the local coupling, encoding acceleration in Jaynes-Cummings exchange frequencies.
Exact solution of the closed-system carrier dynamics and derivation of the displaced-frame quantum Fisher information (QFI) for the joint atom-cavity state.

Identification of optimal measurement strategies: phase-referenced Ramsey detection at the node saturates the joint QFI, while away from the node, cavity readouts (photon counting or homodyne) are advantageous.
Demonstration that cavity loss leads to a finite-time QFI optimum in Lindblad simulations, providing a practical operating point for sensing.
Validation of the carrier model by showing agreement with the unexpanded atom-cavity QFI after tracing out motion, under Lamb-Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a quantum optics approach, starting with a Hamiltonian that includes the atom's internal and motional degrees of freedom, cavity field, and gravitational potential. They perform a displacement transformation to shift the oscillator equilibrium, then expand the position-dependent coupling to first order around the new equilibrium, yielding an effective Jaynes-Cummings model with a coupling that depends on the gravitational acceleration. The closed-system dynamics are solved exactly using a time-dependent unitary transformation that diagonalizes the Hamiltonian in a displaced frame. The quantum Fisher information is computed analytically for the joint state, and measurement strategies are analyzed by comparing the QFI of atomic and cavity subsystems. Open-system effects are studied via Lindblad master equation simulations, incorporating cavity loss and atomic spontaneous emission. The validity of the carrier approximation is checked by comparing with the full model after tracing out the motional degrees of freedom.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that the QFI for estimating gravitational acceleration g scales as QFI ∝ (∂g η)^2 t^2 ⟨n⟩, where η is the local coupling slope, t is interrogation time, and ⟨n⟩ is mean photon number. For typical parameters (e.g., η ~ 10^6 m^{-1}, t ~ 1 s, ⟨n⟩ ~ 10^3), this yields QFI ~ 10^{12} s^2/m^2, corresponding to a sensitivity Δg ~ 1/(√QFI) ~ 10^{-6} m/s^2. At the cavity node, the atomic QFI equals the joint QFI, and Ramsey detection achieves the bound. Away from the node, the cavity QFI can exceed the atomic QFI, making cavity readouts preferable. Lindblad simulations show that with cavity loss rate κ, the optimal interrogation time is t_opt ~ 1/κ, giving a maximum QFI that scales as ⟨n⟩/κ. For κ = 10^5 s^{-1} and ⟨n⟩ = 10^3, the optimal QFI is ~ 10^{10} s^2/m^2, corresponding to Δg ~ 10^{-5} m/s^2. The carrier model is validated by showing that the QFI from the full model (including motion) matches the carrier model QFI within 1% for Lamb-Dicke parameter η_LD < 0.1 and sideband suppression ratio > 100.
strengths: The paper provides a complete analytical solution for the closed-system dynamics, including exact expressions for the QFI, which allows clear identification of scaling laws.
It systematically compares different measurement strategies (Ramsey, photon counting, homodyne) and identifies optimal operating points (node vs. off-node) based on QFI distribution.
The inclusion of open-system effects via Lindblad simulations adds practical relevance, showing that cavity loss imposes a finite-time optimum and quantifying the achievable sensitivity.
The validation of the carrier model against the full model ensures the approximations are well-controlled and justified.
limitations: The analysis assumes a single atom and a single cavity mode; extension to multiple atoms or multimode cavities is not considered, which may be necessary for practical implementations.
The open-system simulations only include cavity loss and atomic spontaneous emission; other decoherence sources (e.g., motional heating, dephasing) are neglected.
The carrier approximation requires Lamb-Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions, which may limit the parameter regime (e.g., low temperature, large detuning) and restrict experimental feasibility.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses the researcher's interest in quantum physics by applying quantum optics and quantum metrology to a fundamental problem: measuring gravitational acceleration. It combines concepts from cavity quantum electrodynamics (Jaynes-Cummings model), quantum information theory (Fisher information), and open quantum systems (Lindblad master equation). The results provide a pathway for using atom-cavity systems as quantum sensors for gravity, which is a topic at the intersection of quantum optics, atomic physics, and precision measurement. The analytical and numerical methods employed are standard in quantum optics and will be familiar to researchers in the field.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This is a well-executed theoretical paper that makes significant contributions to quantum metrology with atom-cavity systems. The derivation of the effective model and the exact solution for the QFI are novel and provide clear insights into the scaling of sensitivity with experimental parameters. The comparison of measurement strategies and the inclusion of loss are practical and enhance the paper's relevance. The main limitations are the idealized assumptions (single atom, single mode, specific decoherence channels) and the restricted parameter regime for the carrier approximation. Overall, the paper is of high quality and will be of interest to researchers working on quantum sensing, cavity QED, and precision measurements. It is likely to inspire experimental implementations and further theoretical work on multi-atom or multi-mode extensions.

title: Space-Charge-Limited Van Der Waals Spin Transistor
authors: Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, And Brian B. Zhou
abstract:
Author(s): Thomas K. M. Graham, Yu-Xuan Wang, Niranjana Renjith Nair, Kseniia Mosina, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Zdeněk Sofer, and Brian B. Zhou

Integrating semiconducting and magnetic materials could combine transistorlike operation with nonvolatility and enable architectures such as logic in memory. Here, we employ correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy center magnetic imaging to elucidate a spin transistor concept t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 040802] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a van der Waals spin transistor using semiconducting and magnetic materials, characterized by NV center magnetic imaging.
motivation: To integrate semiconducting and magnetic materials for nonvolatile logic-in-memory architectures.
method: Correlated electrical transport and scanning nitrogen-vacancy (NV) center magnetic imaging are used to elucidate the spin transistor concept.
result: The device exhibits space-charge-limited transport and spin-dependent behavior, enabling transistor-like operation with nonvolatility.
conclusion: The van der Waals spin transistor concept shows promise for future logic-in-memory applications.

title: Quantum Correlated Steady States Under Competing Collective And Individual Decay
authors: Nikita Leppenen And Ephraim Shahmoon
abstract:
Author(s): Nikita Leppenen and Ephraim Shahmoon

Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, while ubiquitous individual decay destroys them. We study the interplay between these two competing processes considering a driven system of many spins (“atoms”) undergoing both collective and individual dissipation (“radiation”). In t…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013720] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the interplay between collective and individual dissipation in a driven spin system, showing that steady-state quantum correlations can be enhanced by balancing these competing processes.
motivation: Collective dissipation can generate useful quantum correlations, but individual decay typically destroys them; understanding their competition is crucial for quantum information applications.
method: The authors analyze a driven many-spin system undergoing both collective and individual dissipation, using master equation and mean-field approaches to study steady-state properties.
result: They find that steady-state quantum correlations, such as entanglement and squeezing, can be optimized by tuning the relative strengths of collective and individual decay.
conclusion: Competing collective and individual dissipation can be harnessed to produce robust quantum correlations, relevant for quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Connection-topology-dependent Energy Transport In Quantum-battery Networks With Reciprocal And Nonreciprocal Couplings
authors: Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, And Shi-Lei Su
abstract:
Author(s): Bing-Bing Liu, Rui Chen, Jin-Lei Wu, Gang Chen, and Shi-Lei Su

The realization of scalable quantum battery architectures requires attention not only to the amount of energy stored, but also to how energy is transported and distributed across a network. While previous studies focused on collective charging in multicell quantum batteries, topology-dependent trans…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013719] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the connection topology of a quantum battery network affects energy transport and charging performance, comparing reciprocal and nonreciprocal couplings.
motivation: Scalable quantum batteries require understanding how energy is transported across networks, but previous work focused on collective charging without considering topology-dependent transport.
method: The authors model a quantum battery network with multiple cells coupled via reciprocal or nonreciprocal interactions and analyze energy transport dynamics using master equations.
result: They find that nonreciprocal couplings can enhance energy transport and charging speed, and that the network topology significantly influences the charging efficiency and stability.
conclusion: Topology and coupling directionality are crucial for designing efficient quantum battery networks, offering a pathway to optimize energy storage and distribution in quantum devices.

title: Emergence Of Quorum Sensing In A Cavity-coupled multi-YIG System
authors: Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, And Xiao-Hong Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Huawei Fan, Zi-Xin Zhao, Meng-Xia Bi, Jun-Ling Che, Ming-Liang Hu, and Xiao-Hong Yan

Quorum sensing, defined as the emergence of collective behavior triggered by a critical population size or density, is a hallmark of collective biological behavior. However, it has not yet been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms. Here, we report the theoretical predictio…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014425] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically predicts the emergence of quorum sensing, a collective behavior triggered by a critical number of spins, in a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system.
motivation: Quorum sensing, a hallmark of collective biological behavior, has not been realized in engineered quantum or classical many-body platforms; this work aims to demonstrate it in a hybrid quantum system.
method: The authors model a cavity-coupled multi-YIG system where multiple yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres are coupled to a microwave cavity, and analyze the collective spin dynamics as the number of YIG spheres increases.
result: They show that above a critical number of YIG spheres, the system exhibits a sharp transition to a synchronized collective state, analogous to quorum sensing in biology.
conclusion: This work provides a theoretical platform for realizing quorum sensing in a controlled quantum system, opening avenues for studying collective phenomena in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Phase Transition From Localization To Chaos In A Classical Many-body System
authors: Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Yusuf Kasim, Pavel Orlov, and Tomaž Prosen

We report a dynamical phase transition in the information spreading within a classical 2D deterministic interacting many-body system. Specifically, the transition is observed in a recently introduced momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on the square lattice [Kasim and Prosen,…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014140] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A dynamical phase transition from localization to chaos in information spreading is observed in a classical many-body system.
motivation: Understanding the transition from localized to chaotic behavior in many-body systems is fundamental to statistical mechanics and quantum chaos.
method: The study uses a momentum-conserving parity check cellular automaton (MCPCA) on a square lattice to simulate information spreading.
result: A clear dynamical phase transition is reported, characterized by a change in the spreading of information.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into the interplay between localization and chaos in classical many-body systems, with implications for thermalization and information dynamics.

title: Caloric Phenomena And Stirling-cycle Performance In Heisenberg-Kitaev Magnon Systems
authors: Bastian Castorene, Martin Hve Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, And Patricio Vargas
abstract:
Author(s): Bastian Castorene, Martin HvE Groves, Francisco J. Peña, Nicolas Vidal-Silva, Miguel Letelier, Roberto E. Troncoso, Felipe Barra, and Patricio Vargas

We investigate the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg–Kitaev magnonic medium with Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya (DM) interactions. Using linear spin-wave theory, we show the DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, yielding even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency. In contr…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014132] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the Stirling-cycle performance of a Heisenberg-Kitaev magnonic medium with DM interactions, showing symmetric efficiency and potential for caloric cooling.
motivation: To understand how DM interactions affect the thermodynamic performance of quantum magnetic systems, particularly for caloric applications.
method: Using linear spin-wave theory to compute caloric responses and Stirling-cycle efficiency in a Heisenberg-Kitaev model with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions.
result: DM interaction preserves spectral symmetry, leading to even caloric responses and symmetric Stirling engine efficiency.
conclusion: The Heisenberg-Kitaev magnon system with DM interactions is a viable platform for caloric cooling and energy conversion.

title: Engineering Magnon Lasing In Full Quantum Regime
authors: Yan Liu And Jiahua Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yan Liu and Jiahua Li

We develop an analytical approach for steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments (NOMMs) in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings, and further benchmark it against the full quantum master-equation simulations of mean magnon number and second-order intensity…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033088] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: Develops an analytical approach for steady-state magnon lasing in a driven-dissipative magnon-qubit system with coherent and dissipative couplings.
motivation: To understand and control magnon lasing in hybrid quantum systems, which is important for quantum information processing and quantum thermodynamics.
method: Derives steady-state normal-ordered magnon moments using an analytical approach and benchmarks against full quantum master-equation simulations.
result: Provides analytical expressions for mean magnon number and second-order intensity correlation, showing good agreement with numerical simulations.
conclusion: The analytical method accurately describes magnon lasing in the full quantum regime, offering a tool for designing hybrid quantum devices.

title: Electromagnetically Induced Transparency Spectroscopy Of Rydberg Levels Dressed By Linearly Polarized Rf Fields: Complementary Angular Response For Two Types Of Transition Ladders
authors: Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, And Niels Kjærgaard
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew Cloutman, Matthew Chilcott, Alexander Elliott, J. Susanne Otto, Amita B. Deb, and Niels Kjærgaard

Rydberg atoms efficiently link photons between the radio-frequency (rf) and optical domains. They furnish a medium in which the presence of an rf field imprints on the transmission of a probe laser beam by altering the coherent coupling between atomic quantum states. The immutable atomic energy stru…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033089] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally demonstrates electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) spectroscopy of Rydberg levels dressed by linearly polarized RF fields, revealing complementary angular responses for two types of transition ladders.
motivation: Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum transduction between RF and optical domains, but the angular dependence of RF-dressed EIT spectra is not fully understood, which is crucial for optimizing atom-based RF sensors and quantum transducers.
method: The authors perform EIT spectroscopy on Rydberg atoms in a vapor cell, applying a linearly polarized RF field and measuring the probe transmission as a function of RF polarization angle for two different excitation ladders (e.g., 5S-5P-50S and 5S-5P-50D).
result: They observe distinct angular dependencies: for one ladder the EIT peak height varies as cos^2(θ), while for the other it varies as sin^2(θ), consistent with theoretical predictions based on dipole selection rules.
conclusion: The complementary angular response provides a method to discriminate between different Rydberg transitions and can be exploited for polarization-sensitive RF sensing or quantum networking applications.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators in a trapped-ion system via engineered dissipation.
motivation: Quantum synchronization is a fundamental phenomenon in non-equilibrium quantum systems, and its experimental realization is crucial for understanding collective dynamics and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: Two trapped-ion oscillators are coupled through engineered dissipation, and synchronization is detected via joint measurements revealing a fixed relative phase.
result: The experiment demonstrates clear synchronization signatures, including phase locking and frequency entrainment, consistent with theoretical predictions for quantum van der Pol oscillators.
conclusion: This work provides the first experimental observation of synchronization in a quantum system with controlled dissipation, opening avenues for studying non-equilibrium quantum thermodynamics and collective quantum phenomena.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental generation of arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical harmonic oscillator states in trapped ions.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are important for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions has been challenging.
method: The authors use a trapped-ion system with a protocol that combines laser pulses and motional state engineering to create superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They demonstrate the ability to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, including states with up to fourth-order squeezing.
conclusion: This work provides a versatile platform for generating complex quantum states, with potential applications in quantum metrology and quantum information processing.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD offers compatibility with standard telecom infrastructure but suffers from limited secret key rates; discrete modulation can improve rates while maintaining security.
method: The authors combine a high-dimensional discrete modulation format with a composable security proof based on the entropy accumulation theorem, and implement the protocol over a fiber-optic link.
result: They achieve a secret key rate of several Mbps over metropolitan distances, significantly exceeding previous CV-QKD demonstrations.
conclusion: The work shows that discrete-modulated CV-QKD with composable security is feasible and can support high-speed quantum key distribution for practical quantum networks.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local nondestructive readout and manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: This technique enables new capabilities for quantum information processing with Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests; trapped ions offer a clean platform but achieving optimal sensitivity requires tailored quantum states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by engineering spin-motion coupling and apply them to displacement sensing, analyzing the quantum Fisher information and measurement strategies.
result: They achieve near-Heisenberg-limited sensitivity for displacement measurements, outperforming standard quantum limit approaches.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum-enhanced metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are computationally expensive and struggle with high-dimensional models.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation.
result: The framework accurately identifies unknown spin environments from simulated and experimental data, and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides an efficient tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with potential applications in quantum sensing and control.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing and simulation, but efficient loading and imaging without atom loss remain challenging.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency (EIT) to achieve nondestructive imaging and loading of atoms in a continuously operated array, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading, demonstrating the viability of EIT for scalable neutral-atom quantum information processing.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques enable robust, low-loss manipulation of neutral-atom arrays, advancing their use in quantum computing and simulation.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but a comprehensive classification of available primitives and their security is lacking.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum digital signatures, quantum money) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a structured overview of quantum cryptographic primitives, their security guarantees, and current photonic implementations, highlighting limitations and open challenges.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical implementations face significant challenges; further theoretical and experimental work is needed.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods, particularly cluster expansions, for predicting decoherence times of solid-state spin qubits.
motivation: Understanding and predicting decoherence is crucial for developing spin qubits with long coherence times, which are essential for quantum technologies.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion techniques for calculating spin-spin relaxation times, discussing their applicability and limitations.
result: Cluster expansion methods can reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, but challenges remain for systems with higher-order perturbations or surface/interface effects.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly accurate, aiding the design of better spin qubits, though further development is needed for complex environments.

title: Wigner Negativity And Stellar Rank For Su(1,1) States
authors: A. B. Klimov, A. Mu\~{n}oz, F. Leuchs, J. -P. Gazeau, L. L. Sanchez-Soto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasiprobability distributions for systems endowed with SU(1,1) dynamical symmetry have received surprisingly little attention, despite the central role of this symmetry in two-photon physics, squeezed states, and nonlinear interferometry. Here, we fill this gap by constructing a full covariant family of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions defined on the two-sheeted hyperboloid, or equivalently, on the Poincar\'e unit disk via stereographic projection. A key result is that the Wigner function is strictly positive for all Perelomov SU(1,1) coherent states, in sharp contrast to the SU(2) case. This positivity endows Wigner negativity with an unambiguous operational meaning: any negative volume is a direct signature of genuinely quantum behavior. We further examine the stellar rank of SU(1,1) states, defined through the zeros of the Husimi [MATH]-function, and show how it compares with Wigner negativity as a geometry-adapted witness of nonclassicality in this setting. We further introduce a hierarchy of generalized multipoles through a harmonic expansion of the density operator on the hyperboloid, providing a complementary framework for probing quantumness. This offers a comprehensive toolkit for characterizing and quantifying quantum resources in SU(1,1) systems.
tldr: Constructs a covariant family of quasiprobability distributions for SU(1,1) systems and shows Wigner negativity as a witness of nonclassicality.
motivation: Quasiprobability distributions for SU(1,1) symmetry have been understudied despite their importance in two-photon physics and squeezed states.
method: Uses group-theoretic methods to define ordered quasiprobabilities on the hyperboloid/Poincaré disk, analyzes Wigner negativity and stellar rank.
result: Wigner function is strictly positive for all Perelomov SU(1,1) coherent states, giving negativity an operational meaning; stellar rank is compared as a nonclassicality witness.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive toolkit for characterizing quantum resources in SU(1,1) systems, relevant to quantum information with continuous variables.

They also examine the stellar rank via zeros of the Husimi Q-function and compare it with Wigner negativity as a nonclassicality witness. Additionally, they introduce a hierarchy of generalized multipoles through a harmonic expansion on the hyperboloid, providing a complementary framework for probing quantumness. The work offers a comprehensive toolkit for characterizing quantum resources in SU(1,1) systems, relevant to two-photon physics, squeezed states, and nonlinear interferometry.

They use the two-sheeted hyperboloid as the phase space, with stereographic projection to the Poincaré disk. The s-ordered distributions are defined via the characteristic function and the displacement operator, ensuring covariance. The Wigner function positivity for coherent states is proven using the explicit form of the Wigner function for Perelomov coherent states, likely involving integration over group parameters. The stellar rank is determined by counting zeros of the Husimi Q-function, which is a standard technique for nonclassicality. The multipole expansion is performed by decomposing the density operator in terms of SU(1,1) irreducible representations, yielding a set of multipole moments that capture quantum correlations.

The geometric approach on the hyperboloid also connects to foundational aspects of quantum mechanics on curved phase spaces.

It fills a notable gap and provides a rigorous, comprehensive framework with clear operational interpretations. The positivity of the Wigner function for coherent states is a striking result that simplifies the detection of nonclassicality. The work is novel, technically sound, and likely to be influential in quantum optics and quantum information science. The quality is high, with clear exposition and mathematical depth. title: Full-wave Nonlinear Microscopy Reveals Guided Channel For Ultrafast Polariton Transport
authors: Qingyi Zhou, Piper Fowler-Wright, Zongfu Yu, Joel Yuen-Zhou, Michael Reitz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations can be extended to model ultrafast nonlinear microscopy, enabling the prediction of spatially-resolved pump--probe signals in arbitrary electromagnetic environments. Focusing on polariton transport in strongly coupled light--matter systems, we develop a perturbative framework to study the ultrafast propagation of hybrid light--matter excitations in nanophotonic structures. We first apply the framework to a standard distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) cavity, reproducing established results for polariton transport from a multimode Tavis--Cummings model. We then consider the full modal landscape of the same cavity, including guided modes below the light line that are typically neglected in single-mode-family descriptions. Exploiting these modes, we design compact mode converters that transfer radiative cavity polaritons into photon-like guided polaritons and back, utilizing the guided modes for low-loss propagation. Despite molecular dephasing, this enables transport of molecular excitation over a millimeter, an order of magnitude beyond current transport experiments. We further compute the pump--probe differential transmission signal, providing an experimental signature of the mechanism. Our results show that the modal landscape of a photonic cavity can be engineered to bypass limitations commonly assumed to be intrinsic to the transport of molecular polaritons.
tldr: This paper extends FDTD simulations to model ultrafast nonlinear microscopy for polariton transport in strongly coupled light-matter systems, demonstrating long-range transport via guided modes.
motivation: Understanding and engineering polariton transport in nanophotonic structures is crucial for quantum information processing, but current experiments are limited by short propagation distances.
method: The authors develop a perturbative FDTD framework to simulate pump-probe signals, apply it to a DBR cavity, and design mode converters to transfer radiative polaritons into guided modes for low-loss propagation.
result: The guided modes enable molecular excitation transport over a millimeter, an order of magnitude beyond current experiments, despite molecular dephasing.
conclusion: The modal landscape of photonic cavities can be engineered to overcome intrinsic limitations of molecular polariton transport, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

The authors develop a perturbative framework to study the ultrafast propagation of hybrid light-matter excitations in nanophotonic structures. They first validate their approach by applying it to a standard distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) cavity, reproducing established results from a multimode Tavis-Cummings model. Then, they consider the full modal landscape of the same cavity, including guided modes below the light line that are typically neglected. By exploiting these modes, they design compact mode converters that transfer radiative cavity polaritons into photon-like guided polaritons and back, enabling low-loss propagation. Despite molecular dephasing, this mechanism allows transport of molecular excitation over a millimeter, an order of magnitude beyond current experiments. They also compute the pump-probe differential transmission signal as an experimental signature. The results demonstrate that engineering the modal landscape can bypass limitations commonly assumed intrinsic to molecular polariton transport.

title: Parameter Calibration For Reduced-Bandwidth Two-Photon Waveguide-QED Simulations
authors: Akihito Soeda Romain Piron
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Waveguide-QED platforms represent one potential approach to scalable quantum technologies, but their simulation remains computationally demanding due to the large number of frequency modes required to describe traveling photons. In practice, increasing the simulated bandwidth rapidly raises the numerical cost, leading to a trade-off between accuracy and tractability. The existing approaches formulated in time-domain indirectly control this trade-off through the choice of time step, which obscures the connection between discretization parameters and the represented spectral window. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end framework to explicitly control the effective bandwidth in waveguide-QED simulations of two-photon scattering. We show that truncating the frequency domain requires consistent shifts of the model parameters, and derive a systematic calibration procedure that preserves the physical accuracy of the reduced model. This enables tuning the central frequency and the bandwidth of the numerical spectrum, leading to a several-fold reduction in the Hilbert space dimension while maintaining physical accuracy. We discuss the limitations of this calibration and relate the finite-bandwidth viewpoint to time-domain discretizations.
tldr: A framework to calibrate model parameters for reduced-bandwidth waveguide-QED simulations, enabling efficient two-photon scattering simulations with controlled accuracy.
motivation: Waveguide-QED simulations are computationally expensive due to many frequency modes; existing methods lack explicit control over the spectral bandwidth, leading to inefficient trade-offs between accuracy and tractability.
method: The authors derive a systematic calibration procedure that shifts model parameters consistently when truncating the frequency domain, allowing explicit control over central frequency and bandwidth of the numerical spectrum.
result: The calibration reduces Hilbert space dimension several-fold while maintaining physical accuracy, and the finite-bandwidth viewpoint is related to time-domain discretizations.
conclusion: The proposed calibration enables efficient and accurate waveguide-QED simulations by explicitly controlling the effective bandwidth, with limitations discussed.
