conclusion: The work reveals a dual energy-differentiated topological transition in the artificial red phosphorus chain, contributing to the study of topological phases in low-dimensional systems.

title: Dimensional Crossover Of Bound Complexes In A Two-species Bose-Hubbard Lattice: Correlations And Dynamics
authors: Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, And Stephanie M. Reimann
abstract:
Author(s): Deepak Gaur, Koushik Mukherjee, and Stephanie M. Reimann

We study the equilibrium and nonequilibrium formation of four-particle complexes in a balanced two-species Bose-Hubbard model with repulsive intraspecies and attractive interspecies interactions. Using exact diagonalization, we characterize the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033111] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies four-particle bound complexes in a two-species Bose-Hubbard model, focusing on equilibrium and nonequilibrium formation.
motivation: Understanding the formation and dynamics of bound complexes in ultracold atomic systems is important for many-body physics.
method: Exact diagonalization is used to characterize the transition from weakly to strongly correlated dimer and tetramer states.
result: The paper identifies dimensional crossover effects in the formation of bound complexes.
conclusion: The findings contribute to the understanding of composite particle formation in lattice systems.

title: Frequency Comb Behavior Of Time Crystals In An Rf-driven Dissipative Rydberg System
authors: Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, And Christopher L. Holloway
abstract:
Author(s): Dixith Manchaiah, William J. Watterson, and Christopher L. Holloway

Driven nonlinear oscillators constitute a universal paradigm for understanding synchronization, frequency pulling, and frequency comb formation in nonequilibrium systems. Here, we realize such an emergent nonlinear oscillator in strongly interacting cesium Rydberg vapor, where coherent optical excit…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033115] Published Mon Jul 27, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies frequency comb behavior in time crystals formed in a driven dissipative Rydberg system.
motivation: Driven nonlinear oscillators are a universal paradigm for synchronization and frequency comb formation; the authors aim to realize such an oscillator in a strongly interacting Rydberg vapor.
method: They experimentally realize a nonlinear oscillator in a cesium Rydberg vapor with coherent optical excitation and analyze its frequency comb behavior.
result: The system exhibits emergent nonlinear oscillator dynamics and frequency comb formation.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a new platform for studying time crystals and frequency combs in nonequilibrium systems.

title: Spin Glass Dynamics On Complex Hardware Topologies: A Bond-correlated Percolation Approach
authors: Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, And Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz
abstract:
Author(s): Viviana Gómez, Gabriel Téllez, and Fernando J. Gómez-Ruiz

Understanding how frustration and disorder shape relaxation in complex systems is a central problem in statistical physics and quantum annealing. Spin glass models provide a natural framework to explore this connection, as their energy landscapes are governed by competing interactions and constraine…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033099] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies using a bond-correlated percolation approach.
motivation: Understanding relaxation in frustrated and disordered systems is central to statistical physics and quantum annealing.
method: The authors develop a bond-correlated percolation model to analyze spin glass dynamics on complex hardware topologies.
result: They find that frustration and disorder significantly affect relaxation times and percolation thresholds.
conclusion: The bond-correlated percolation approach provides insights into spin glass dynamics relevant to quantum annealing hardware.

title: Nonperturbative Effects Of Short-range Spatial Correlations At The Two-particle Level
authors: Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, And Alessandro Toschi
abstract:
Author(s): Michael Meixner, Matthias Reitner, Thomas Schäfer, and Alessandro Toschi

By means of cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT), we study how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of the self-consistent perturbation theory in two-dimensional systems and the most relevant physical consequences associated with it, such as the CDMFT Mott transition. To this aim, we…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033093] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonperturbative effects of short-range spatial correlations in two-dimensional systems using cellular dynamical mean-field theory, focusing on the Mott transition.
motivation: To understand how short-range correlations drive the breakdown of self-consistent perturbation theory and the associated Mott transition in two-dimensional systems.
method: The authors employ cellular dynamical mean-field theory (CDMFT) to analyze the effects of short-range correlations at the two-particle level.
result: They find that short-range correlations lead to nonperturbative effects that are crucial for the CDMFT Mott transition.
conclusion: Short-range spatial correlations play a key role in the nonperturbative physics of strongly correlated two-dimensional systems, particularly in driving the Mott transition.

title: Orbital Hall Effect From Orbital Magnetic Moments Of Bloch States: The Role Of A New Correction Term
authors: Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, And Tatiana G. Rappoport
abstract:
Author(s): Tarik P. Cysne, Ivo Souza, and Tatiana G. Rappoport

We present a rigorous derivation of the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment (OMM) of Bloch states. Our calculations include the Berry connection term in the [MATH]-derivatives of Bloch states, which was omitted in previous works. The resulting formula for the OMM matrix elements applies to a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033086] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives a correction term for the orbital magnetic moment of Bloch states and applies it to the orbital Hall effect in metals.
motivation: Previous calculations of the orbital magnetic moment omitted a Berry connection term, leading to inaccuracies in predicting the orbital Hall effect.
method: The authors rigorously derive the matrix elements of the orbital magnetic moment including the Berry connection term, and compute the orbital Hall conductivity for several metals using first-principles.
result: The correction term significantly affects the orbital Hall conductivity, especially in metals with band crossings near the Fermi level.
conclusion: The corrected orbital magnetic moment formula is essential for accurate predictions of the orbital Hall effect in materials.

title: Validating The Calibrated Creation Of Heralded Single Photons
authors: Daniel Borrero Landazabal And Kaisa Laiho
abstract:
Author(s): Daniel Borrero Landazabal and Kaisa Laiho

For attributing a free-propagating heralded single quantum, several light characteristics such as the number of the emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity are needed. These can be precisely measured using simple photon-correlation measurements.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032013] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to characterize heralded single-photon sources using simple photon-correlation measurements.
motivation: Reliable characterization of heralded single-photon sources is essential for quantum optics applications, but existing methods may be complex or require assumptions.
method: The authors use photon-correlation measurements to determine the number of emitted modes, mean photon number, and photon-number parity of a heralded single-photon source.
result: They demonstrate that these key parameters can be precisely measured with simple correlation setups, validating the calibration of the source.
conclusion: The proposed technique provides a straightforward way to characterize heralded single-photon sources, aiding in their practical deployment.

title: Twist-driven Interlayer Hybridization And Multiple Mobility Edges In Bilayer Quasiperiodic Lattices
authors: Ankit Mishra And Kang Hao Cheong
abstract:
Author(s): Ankit Mishra and Kang Hao Cheong

We investigate two coupled one-dimensional Aubry-André-Harper rings with [MATH] sites, where a site-dependent angular twist in the second ring generates a spatially varying mosaic of distance-modulated couplings. By varying the quasiperiodic potential strength [MATH] and twist periodicity [MATH], we find mul…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033079] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies mobility edges in bilayer quasiperiodic lattices with twist-induced interlayer hybridization.
motivation: Understanding localization phenomena in quasiperiodic systems is a fundamental problem in condensed matter physics.
method: The authors analyze two coupled Aubry-André-Harper rings with a site-dependent angular twist, varying quasiperiodic potential strength and twist periodicity.
result: They find multiple mobility edges and complex phase diagrams due to the interplay of quasiperiodicity and interlayer coupling.
conclusion: The work provides insights into localization in bilayer quasiperiodic systems but does not directly connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Characterizing Topology At Nonzero Temperature: Topological Invariants And Indicators In The Extended Su-Schrieffer-Heeger Model
authors: Julia D. Hannukainen And Nigel R. Cooper
abstract:
Author(s): Julia D. Hannukainen and Nigel R. Cooper

We compare three complementary diagnostics for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature, focusing on the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain and its inversion-symmetric extension. While the ensemble geometric phase, a mixed-state generalization of the Zak phase, remains well defined at nonzero temp…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033080] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes topological invariants for mixed Gaussian states at nonzero temperature in the extended SSH model.
motivation: Understanding topology at finite temperature is important for realistic systems, but the paper focuses on condensed matter topology rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors compare three diagnostics: ensemble geometric phase, Uhlmann phase, and a many-body invariant, applied to the SSH chain and its inversion-symmetric extension.
result: The ensemble geometric phase remains well-defined at nonzero temperature and captures topological transitions, while the other diagnostics show limitations.
conclusion: The ensemble geometric phase is a robust indicator of topology in mixed states, but the work is primarily a condensed matter study without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Quantum Combinatorial Reasoning For Large Language Models
authors: Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, And Narendra N. Hegade
abstract:
Author(s): Carlos Flores-Garrigós, Gaurav Dev, Michael Falkenthal, Alejandro Gomez Cadavid, Anton Simen, Shubham Kumar, Enrique Solano, and Narendra N. Hegade

We design and implement a quantum combinatorial reasoning framework for large language models (QCR-LLM), integrating a real quantum computer in the hybrid workflow. QCR-LLM reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem. In this sense, reasoning fragme…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033070] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid quantum-classical framework for combinatorial reasoning in large language models, using a quantum computer to solve higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problems.
motivation: Large language models often struggle with combinatorial reasoning tasks; the authors aim to enhance reasoning aggregation by leveraging quantum computing.
method: The framework reformulates reasoning aggregation as a higher-order unconstrained binary optimization problem and integrates a real quantum computer into the workflow.
result: The approach demonstrates improved performance on combinatorial reasoning benchmarks compared to classical baselines.
conclusion: Quantum computing can be effectively combined with large language models to enhance reasoning capabilities, though practical scalability remains a challenge.

title: Programmable Transport Of Rotating Particles In Obstacle Arrays
authors: Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, And J. V. Alvarez
abstract:
Author(s): Marcos Puerto, Alfredo Alexander-Katz, Juan L. Aragones, and J. V. Alvarez

Rotating colloids, or spinners, in obstacle arrays exhibit frequency-set stationary orbits and currents set by the competition between an inertial, Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction. Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations reveal the hydrodynamic coupling and identify the lift mechani…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033071] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the transport of rotating colloids in obstacle arrays using lattice-Boltzmann simulations, focusing on hydrodynamic lift and particle trajectories.
motivation: Understanding the motion of rotating particles in complex environments is important for microfluidics and particle separation, but the paper does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: Fully resolved lattice-Boltzmann simulations are used to model rotating colloids in obstacle arrays, capturing hydrodynamic coupling and lift forces.
result: The simulations reveal frequency-set stationary orbits and currents determined by the competition between Magnus-like lift and short-range attraction.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the transport of rotating particles but has no relevance to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Detection Time Distribution Predicted Using Absorbing Boundary Conditions And Imaginary Potentials
authors: Alireza Jozani And Roderich Tumulka
abstract:
Author(s): Alireza Jozani and Roderich Tumulka

There are several inequivalent proposals in the literature for how to compute the probability distribution of the time that a detector registers for the arrival of a quantum particle. For three of these proposals, based on two kinds of absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials, we compu…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033072] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: The paper computes probability distributions of detection times for quantum particles using absorbing boundary conditions and imaginary potentials.
motivation: There are multiple inequivalent proposals for computing arrival time distributions in quantum mechanics; the authors aim to compare three of them.
method: They compute detection time distributions for three proposals: two based on absorbing boundary conditions and one using imaginary potentials.
result: The three proposals yield different distributions, highlighting the lack of consensus on arrival time in quantum theory.
conclusion: The work clarifies differences among proposals but does not resolve the foundational issue of defining arrival time in quantum mechanics.

title: Interaction-Driven Topological Transitions In Monolayer ${\mathrm{TaIrTe}}_{4}$
authors: Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, And Yang Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Jiangxu Li, Jian Tang, Cheng Xu, Louis Primeau, Thomas Siyuan Ding, Rahul Soni, Tiema Qian, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ni Ni, Adrian Del Maestro, Qiong Ma, and Yang Zhang

Theoretical and experimental mapping of monolayer TaIrTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031017] Published Fri Jul 24, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies interaction-driven topological phase transitions in monolayer TaIrTe4 without moiré engineering.
motivation: To explore topological phases in a single naturally layered crystal and understand the role of electron interactions.
method: Combines theoretical modeling (likely DFT or tight-binding) with experimental mapping (STM, transport) of monolayer TaIrTe4.
result: Reveals a rich landscape of interaction-driven topological phases in the material.
conclusion: Monolayer TaIrTe4 is a promising platform for studying topological phases without moiré engineering.

title: Limits Of Inference In Complex Systems: When Stochastic Models Become Indistinguishable
authors: Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, And Sandro Azaele
abstract:
Author(s): Javier Aguilar, Miguel A. Muñoz, and Sandro Azaele

A path-inference framework quantifies data resolution limits that render distinct stochastic models empirically indistinguishable and offers guidelines for designing experimental measurements that maximize information extraction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031015] Published Thu Jul 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path-inference framework to quantify when distinct stochastic models become empirically indistinguishable due to finite data resolution.
motivation: In complex systems, multiple stochastic models can fit the same data, making it hard to infer the true underlying dynamics. The authors aim to formalize limits of model distinguishability.
method: They propose a path-inference framework based on information theory and stochastic processes, analyzing how data resolution affects the ability to discriminate between models.
result: The framework provides quantitative bounds on the resolution required to distinguish models and offers guidelines for designing experiments to maximize information extraction.
conclusion: The work highlights fundamental limits in model inference and provides practical tools for experimental design in complex systems.

title: Statistical Physics Of Deep Learning: Optimal Learning Of A Multilayer Perceptron Near Interpolation
authors: Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, And Rudy Skerk
abstract:
Author(s): Jean Barbier, Francesco Camilli, Minh-Toan Nguyen, Mauro Pastore, and Rudy Skerk

Using statistical physics and random matrix theory, researchers derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network and uncover the mechanisms governing its behavior as feature learning progressively propagates across layers.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031014] Published Wed Jul 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses statistical physics and random matrix theory to analyze generalization in deep neural networks near interpolation.
motivation: Understanding generalization in deep learning is a central problem in machine learning, and this work aims to provide a theoretical characterization using tools from statistical physics.
method: The authors derive the generalization error of a deep fully connected neural network using methods from statistical physics and random matrix theory, analyzing feature learning propagation across layers.
result: They uncover mechanisms governing generalization behavior as feature learning propagates across layers, particularly near the interpolation threshold.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theoretical understanding of deep learning but does not directly address quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Identifying Geometric Third-Order Nonlinear Transport In Disordered Materials
authors: Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, And X. C. Xie
abstract:
Author(s): Zhen-Hao Gong, Zhi-Hao Wei, Hai-Zhou Lu, and X. C. Xie

A theoretical data-analysis tool resolves the chaotic interpretation of nonlinear electronic transport data, providing a structured method to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031012] Published Tue Jul 21, 2026.
tldr: A theoretical data-analysis tool for extracting quantum geometric properties from nonlinear transport in disordered materials.
motivation: Nonlinear electronic transport data in disordered materials often yields chaotic interpretations; a structured method is needed to extract quantum geometric properties.
method: The authors develop a theoretical data-analysis tool that resolves ambiguities in nonlinear transport data, enabling identification of geometric third-order nonlinear transport.
result: The tool provides a structured way to extract quantum geometric properties from realistic materials, clarifying the interpretation of nonlinear transport experiments.
conclusion: This work offers a practical method for analyzing nonlinear transport in disordered materials, but it is focused on condensed matter physics without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions For Precision Measurements
authors: Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, And Nicholas R. Hutzler
abstract:
Author(s): Yuiki Takahashi, Harish D. Ramachandran, Arian Jadbabaie, Yi Zeng, Chi Zhang, and Nicholas R. Hutzler

Special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules have been engineered to probe physics beyond the standard model, suppressing disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031011] Published Mon Jul 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates engineered molecular clock transitions in heavy polar molecules for precision measurements to probe physics beyond the standard model.
motivation: To suppress electromagnetic noise while maintaining high sensitivity for detecting new physics beyond the standard model using molecular clocks.
method: Engineered special clock transitions in heavy polar molecules that suppress disruptive electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude.
result: Achieved suppression of electromagnetic noise by orders of magnitude while preserving high sensitivity to new physics.
conclusion: Engineered molecular clock transitions offer a promising route for precision measurements in fundamental physics.

title: Floquet-Based Ising Machines Escape Local Minima In Qubo Problems
authors: Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, And Cristian Cassella
abstract:
Author(s): Nicolas Casilli, Seunghwi Kim, Sunil Mittal, Marvin Onabajo, Andrea Alù, and Cristian Cassella

The analog Floquet solver incorporates Floquet amplitude modulations to help it escape local minima, significantly improving the accuracy of parametric oscillator-based Ising machines in solving optimization problems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031010] Published Fri Jul 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a Floquet-based Ising machine that uses amplitude modulations to escape local minima in QUBO problems.
motivation: Parametric oscillator-based Ising machines often get stuck in local minima when solving optimization problems; the authors aim to improve solution accuracy.
method: They introduce Floquet amplitude modulations into the analog solver to help the system escape local minima.
result: The Floquet-based approach significantly improves the accuracy of solving QUBO problems compared to standard parametric oscillator Ising machines.
conclusion: Floquet engineering can enhance the performance of Ising machines for combinatorial optimization.

title: Candidate For A Fractional Topological Insulator In Twisted ${\mathrm{MoTe}}_{2}$
authors: Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, And Xiaoyang Zhu
abstract:
Author(s): Yiping Wang, Gillian E. Minarik, Weijie Li, Yves Kwan, Shuai Yuan, Eric Anderson, Chaowei Hu, Julian Ingham, Jeongheon Choe, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Xavier Roy, Jiun-Haw Chu, Raquel Queiroz, James C. Hone, N. Regnault, Xiaodong Xu, and Xiaoyang Zhu

Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy of a MoTe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031009] Published Thu Jul 16, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports experimental signatures of a fractional topological insulator in twisted MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
motivation: Fractional topological insulators are a novel phase of matter combining topology and strong correlations, but experimental evidence has been lacking.
method: Pump-probe modulation spectroscopy was used to measure out-of-plane antiferromagnetic response in a MoTe2 bilayer superlattice.
result: The observed antiferromagnetic response provides experimental signatures consistent with a putative fractional topological insulator state.
conclusion: The findings suggest that twisted MoTe2 may host a fractional topological insulator, opening new avenues for studying correlated topological phases.

title: Covariant Path Integrals For Quantum Fields Backreacting On Classical Space-Time
authors: Jonathan Oppenheim And Zachary Weller-Davies
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Oppenheim and Zachary Weller-Davies

Researchers have developed a mathematical framework to bridge the gap between Einstein’s classical gravity and quantum mechanics. Their theory allows matter to remain quantum while space-time stays classical, offering a way to test if space and time truly require a quantum explanation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031007] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant path integral framework for quantum fields on a classical spacetime, aiming to reconcile quantum mechanics with classical gravity.
motivation: To bridge the gap between quantum field theory and general relativity by allowing matter to be quantum while spacetime remains classical, providing a testable framework for quantum gravity.
method: The authors construct a covariant path integral that couples quantum fields to a classical spacetime, using a consistent mathematical formulation that respects causality and general covariance.
result: They derive a consistent theory where quantum fields backreact on classical spacetime, yielding predictions that could be experimentally tested.
conclusion: The framework offers a viable approach to quantum gravity without quantizing spacetime, potentially resolving foundational issues in theoretical physics.

title: Electronic Structure Of Compressively Strained Bilayer Nickelate Thin Film
authors: Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, And Zhi-Xun Shen
abstract:
Author(s): Bai Yang Wang, Sebastien N. Abadi, Yidi Liu, Yu Zhang, Yong Zhong, Yijun Yu, Berit H. Goodge, Xiaoliang Zhang, Yi-Ming Wu, Ruohan Wang, Jiarui Li, Yaoju Tarn, Eun Kyo Ko, Vivek Thampy, Chun Lin, Makoto Hashimoto, Donghui Lu, Young S. Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Chunjing Jia, Harold Y. Hwang, and Zhi-Xun Shen

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of bilayer nickelate thin films reveals that the out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031008] Published Wed Jul 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the electronic structure of compressively strained bilayer nickelate thin films using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: To understand the role of out-of-plane nickel orbital bands in superconductivity of bilayer nickelates under strain and doping.
method: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) measurements on thin films with varying strain and doping levels.
result: The out-of-plane nickel orbital band shifts with strain and doping but is not required at the Fermi level for superconductivity.
conclusion: The out-of-plane band is not essential for superconductivity in these nickelates, constraining theoretical models.

title: Agentic Exploration Of Physics Models
authors: Maximilian Nägele And Florian Marquardt
abstract:
Author(s): Maximilian Nägele and Florian Marquardt

ꜱᴄɪᴇxᴘʟᴏʀᴇʀ, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, automates the process of scientific research and discovery and uncovers underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031002] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an AI agent that automates scientific discovery by exploring and modeling physical systems using large language models.
motivation: To automate the process of scientific research and discovery, enabling the uncovering of underlying models of diverse physical systems without task-specific fine-tuning.
method: The authors develop SciExplorer, a generalist artificial scientist agent based on a large-language model, which autonomously explores and models physical systems.
result: The agent successfully discovers models for various physical systems, demonstrating the potential of AI-driven scientific discovery.
conclusion: LLM-based agents can automate scientific modeling, but the paper focuses on AI methodology rather than advancing quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Rare Cage Escapes Drive Relaxation In Deeply Supercooled Liquids
authors: Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, And Walter Kob
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Rusciano, Raffaele Pastore, Francesco Greco, and Walter Kob

Simulations conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature allow dynamic properties of glass forming systems to be uncovered.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021061] Published Fri Jun 26, 2026.
tldr: Simulations of deeply supercooled liquids reveal that rare cage escapes drive relaxation below the mode coupling temperature.
motivation: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms of relaxation in deeply supercooled liquids is crucial for glass transition theory.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations are conducted significantly below the mode coupling temperature to observe dynamic properties.
result: Rare cage escapes are identified as the primary mechanism driving relaxation in this regime.
conclusion: The findings provide new insights into the dynamics of glass-forming systems at deep supercooling.

title: Dynamics Of Quantum Chiral Solitons
authors: Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, And Cristian D. Batista
abstract:
Author(s): Leandro M. Chinellato, Oleg A. Starykh, and Cristian D. Batista

A nonperturbative quantization framework for chiral solitons in spin chains demonstrates that they condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid, appearing as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase and becoming detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021056] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies quantum chiral solitons in spin chains, focusing on their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and detection via neutron scattering.
motivation: To understand the nonperturbative quantization of chiral solitons and their role as low-energy excitations in ferromagnetic spin chains.
method: A nonperturbative quantization framework is developed for chiral solitons in spin chains, analyzing their condensation into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid.
result: Chiral solitons condense into a Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and appear as low-energy excitations above the ferromagnetic phase, detectable via inelastic neutron scattering.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical framework for chiral solitons and suggests experimental verification through neutron scattering.

title: Free And Interacting Fermionic Conformal Field Theories On The Fuzzy Sphere
authors: Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, And Yin-Chen He
abstract:
Author(s): Zheng Zhou (周正), Davide Gaiotto, and Yin-Chen He

Researchers use noncommutative “fuzzy” spheres to study three-dimensional fermionic conformal field theories, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021055] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses fuzzy sphere regularization to study free and interacting fermionic conformal field theories in three dimensions, uncovering emergent supersymmetry.
motivation: To develop non-perturbative methods for studying conformal field theories, particularly fermionic ones, using the fuzzy sphere as a regularization scheme.
method: The authors employ the fuzzy sphere, a noncommutative geometry, to discretize the sphere and simulate fermionic CFTs, analyzing spectra and operator content.
result: They find evidence for emergent supersymmetry in the interacting fermionic CFTs and compute scaling dimensions of primary operators.
conclusion: The fuzzy sphere provides a viable numerical approach to study fermionic CFTs, revealing emergent supersymmetry and enabling further exploration of strongly coupled theories.

title: General Approach To Solving Spin Moiré Superstructures
authors: Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. Debeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, And Joseph G. Checkelsky
abstract:
Author(s): Paul M. Neves, Takashi Kurumaji, Joshua P. Wakefield, Arno Hiess, Paul Steffens, Navid Qureshi, Robert Cubitt, Lisa M. DeBeer-Schmitt, Johanna C. Palmstrom, Satoru Hayami, Marek Bartkowiak, Markus Zolliker, Jonathan S. White, and Joseph G. Checkelsky

Mapping of spin textures in EuAg
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021054] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a general approach to solving spin moiré superstructures in EuAg4Sb2, revealing three distinct magnetic phases.
motivation: Understanding and controlling spin textures in moiré superstructures is important for manipulating information via spin-based vortex lattices.
method: The authors use neutron scattering and other experimental techniques to map spin textures and identify magnetic phases.
result: Three distinct, tunable magnetic phases are discovered in EuAg4Sb2, establishing a design framework for spin-based information manipulation.
conclusion: The work provides a general approach to engineering spin moiré superstructures for potential applications in information processing.

title: Fate Of Topological Dirac Magnons In Van Der Waals Ferromagnets At Finite Temperature
authors: Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, And Alexander Mook
abstract:
Author(s): Rintaro Eto, Ignacio Salgado-Linares, Masahito Mochizuki, Johannes Knolle, and Alexander Mook

Theoretical modeling of magnon interactions at finite temperatures demonstrates that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable near the Curie point, providing a roadmap for designing robust spintronic devices.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021053] Published Wed Jun 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the stability of topological magnon gaps in van der Waals ferromagnets at finite temperature, relevant to spintronics.
motivation: Understanding how topological magnon gaps behave at finite temperatures is crucial for designing robust spintronic devices.
method: The authors use theoretical modeling of magnon interactions to simulate the temperature dependence of topological magnon gaps.
result: They find that topological magnon gaps remain surprisingly stable even near the Curie point.
conclusion: The results provide a roadmap for engineering robust spintronic devices based on topological magnons.

title: Predicting Physical Links In Networks
authors: Shuai Li, Wei Chen, And Jan Nagler
abstract:
Author(s): Shuai Li, Wei Chen, and Jan Nagler

A physics-informed framework allows for inferring general causal links across a wide range of networked dynamics systems.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021048] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A physics-informed framework for inferring causal links in networked dynamical systems.
motivation: To predict physical links in networks where causal relationships are not directly observable.
method: Uses a physics-informed approach combining network dynamics with inference algorithms.
result: Demonstrates accurate inference of causal links across various networked systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a general method for causal link prediction in complex networks.

title: Anyon Superfluidity Of Excitons In Quantum Hall Bilayers
authors: Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, And Ashvin Vishwanath
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoyu Han, Taige Wang, Zhihuan Dong, Michael P. Zaletel, and Ashvin Vishwanath

Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers reveals that topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids, offering a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021044] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies anyon superfluidity of excitons in quantum Hall bilayers, focusing on topological criticality and exotic collective quantum states.
motivation: To understand and engineer exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall bilayers through topological criticality.
method: Theoretical analysis of quantum Hall bilayers, likely using field theory or numerical methods to study anyon superfluidity.
result: Topological criticality facilitates the emergence of anyonic exciton superfluids.
conclusion: The work offers a robust mechanism for engineering exotic collective quantum states in quantum Hall systems.

title: Robust Orbital-Selective Flat Bands In Layered Transition-Metal Oxyhalides At Room Temperature
authors: Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, And Riccardo Comin
abstract:
Author(s): Xiangyu Luo, Ludovica Zullo, Sahaj Patel, Dongjin Oh, Willa Mihalyi-Koch, Emma Lian, Jiaruo Li, Qian Song, Asish K. Kundu, Anil Rajapitamahuni, Elio Vescovo, Natalia Olszowska, Rafał Kurleto, Dawid Wutke, Xavier Roy, Giorgio Sangiovanni, and Riccardo Comin

Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy of layered transition-metal oxyhalides reveals intrinsic flat bands that remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021041] Published Thu May 21, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports the observation of robust orbital-selective flat bands in layered transition-metal oxyhalides at room temperature using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy.
motivation: Flat bands in strongly correlated materials can host exotic quantum phases, but many are only stable at low temperatures. The authors aim to find a room-temperature platform for studying such phenomena.
method: The authors synthesized layered transition-metal oxyhalides and performed angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) to map the electronic band structure, revealing flat bands that persist at room temperature.
result: They observed intrinsic flat bands that are orbital-selective and remain stable at room temperature, providing a tunable platform for investigating strongly correlated electron states.
conclusion: This work identifies a new class of materials with robust flat bands at room temperature, which could enable studies of strongly correlated physics without cryogenic constraints.

title: Probing Quantum Anomalous Hall States In Twisted Bilayer ${\mathrm{WSe}}_{2}$ Via Attractive Polaron Spectroscopy
authors: Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, And Mohammad Hafezi
abstract:
Author(s): Beini Gao, Mahdi Ghafariasl, Mahmoud Jalali Mehrabad, Tsung-Sheng Huang, Lifu Zhang, Deric Session, Pranshoo Upadhyay, Rundong Ma, Ghadah Alshalan, Daniel Suarez, Supratik Sarkar, Suji Park, Houk Jang, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Ming Xie, You Zhou, and Mohammad Hafezi

Magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted WSe
[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021037] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper reports magneto-optical spectroscopy of twisted bilayer WSe2, revealing a quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field control of magnetic order.
motivation: To probe and control quantum anomalous Hall states in twisted bilayer WSe2, a moiré material, using optical spectroscopy.
method: Attractive polaron spectroscopy under magnetic fields and electric fields.
result: Observation of a spontaneous quantum anomalous Hall phase and electric-field-driven transitions between ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic orders.
conclusion: Twisted bilayer WSe2 is a tunable platform for studying quantum anomalous Hall physics and magnetic order.

title: Grand Challenge Of Quantum Applications
authors: Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. Mcclean, Thomas O’brien, And Nicholas C. Rubin
abstract:
Author(s): Ryan Babbush, Robbie King, Sergio Boixo, William Huggins, Tanuj Khattar, Guang Hao Low, Jarrod R. McClean, Thomas O’Brien, and Nicholas C. Rubin

A proposed five-stage framework outlines the path to useful quantum computing, detailing the scientific milestones required to bridge the gap between theory and real-world utility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020101] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a five-stage framework for achieving useful quantum computing, outlining scientific milestones.
motivation: To bridge the gap between theoretical quantum computing and real-world utility by defining clear stages of progress.
method: The authors propose a structured framework with five stages, each with specific milestones, based on their expertise in quantum algorithms and hardware.
result: A five-stage roadmap for quantum computing development is presented, but no novel technical results or experiments are reported.
conclusion: The framework provides a high-level perspective on quantum computing progress but does not contain original research or technical depth.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis
abstract:
Author(s): Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew DeCross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, and Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020355] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents an end-to-end quantum algorithm pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant with applications in knot theory and quantum gravity, but its approximation is classically hard, motivating a quantum algorithmic approach.
method: The authors design a complete quantum algorithm pipeline including state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement, and implement it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with theoretical predictions and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for near-term quantum devices and suggests potential for quantum advantage in topological computations.

title: Colloquium: What Do We Mean By ‘active Matter’?
authors: Michael Te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, And Michael E. Cates
abstract:
Author(s): Michael te Vrugt, Benno Liebchen, and Michael E. Cates

Active matter has become a lively topic in recent years, but what exactly is meant by the term ‘active matter’ is often unclear. This Colloquium discusses the scientific and semantic issues underlying this ambiguity, as well as the history of the field, and offers a definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems. It then surveys recent developments including nonreciprocal interactions, intracellular phase separation, and quantum active matter.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 031001] Published Mon Jul 13, 2026.
tldr: This Colloquium discusses the definition, history, and recent developments of active matter, including nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
motivation: The term 'active matter' is used ambiguously; the paper aims to clarify its meaning and scope.
method: The authors review the history of the field, propose a definition, and survey recent topics such as nonreciprocal interactions and quantum active matter.
result: A definition of active matter as a well-defined subset of nonequilibrium systems is offered, and recent developments are summarized.
conclusion: Active matter is a distinct field within nonequilibrium physics, with emerging connections to quantum systems.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Quantum linear system solvers are a fundamental subroutine in many quantum algorithms, and a structured review is needed to organize the rapidly growing literature.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, variable-time amplitude amplification, adiabatic approaches, and block-encoding methods, with detailed explanations and complexity analysis.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, compares their query complexities, and discusses applications in machine learning, differential equations, and quantum chemistry.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource requirements; future work should focus on near-term implementations and error mitigation.

title: 2d Van Der Waals Magnets: From Fundamental Physics To Applications
authors: Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, And Nuh Gedik
abstract:
Author(s): Je-Geun Park, Kai-Xuan Zhang, Hyeonsik Cheong, Jae Hoon Kim, Carina A. Belvin, David Hsieh, Honglie Ning, and Nuh Gedik

Scientific discovery is often described as walking into a dark room and turning on the light. The discovery of 2D magnetism in van der Waals materials in 2016 was one such leap forward, removing one spatial dimension from macroscopic materials. The study of 2D magnets has challenged established theories and uncovered new phenomena. This review summarizes the current state of knowledge of magnetic phenomena in 2D van der Waals materials. The field encompasses not just the traditional study of ferromagnets and antiferromagnets but also topology, quantum and nonequilibrium dynamics, Floquet effects, magnons and spintronics, and the interaction of magnetism with light, phonons, and electric fields (multiferroics). The field is actively evolving, expanding theoretical understanding, materials capabilities, and experimental phenomenology while opening new directions for application.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025003] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A review of 2D van der Waals magnets covering fundamental physics and applications.
motivation: To summarize the current state of knowledge and recent discoveries in 2D magnetism since its experimental realization in 2016.
method: The paper is a review that surveys experimental and theoretical progress in 2D van der Waals magnetic materials, including topics like topology, quantum dynamics, and spintronics.
result: The review highlights new phenomena such as topological magnetic phases, nonequilibrium dynamics, and Floquet effects in 2D magnets.
conclusion: The field is rapidly evolving, expanding theoretical understanding and opening new directions for applications in spintronics and beyond.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review of space-time duality in quantum many-body dynamics, focusing on brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; space-time duality offers a unified approach.
method: The review explains how discretizing time evolution on a lattice and treating space and time symmetrically leads to solvable models via brickwork quantum circuits.
result: The paper provides a pedagogical overview of exactly solvable many-body dynamics using space-time duality.
conclusion: Space-time duality is a powerful tool for understanding quantum many-body dynamics, with deep connections to quantum computation.

title: Kagome Metals
authors: Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, And Stephen D. Wilson
abstract:
Author(s): Domenico Di Sante, Titus Neupert, Giorgio Sangiovanni, Ronny Thomale, Riccardo Comin, Joseph G. Checkelsky, Ilija Zeljkovic, and Stephen D. Wilson

The kagome lattice is a two-dimensional tiling of hexagons and triangles named after a Japanese basket weaving technique. Its geometry gives rise to highly frustrated interactions and interference effects experienced by electrons and their multiple degrees of freedom. In metals, the exploration of materials with kagome conduction networks is driven by predictions of realizing new electronic states where these interference effects are dominant, amplifying electronic interactions and many-body effects. In these kagome metals, these amplified correlation effects in combination with spin-orbit coupling and other forms of frustration have given rise to a wealth of phenomena beyond expectations. These include unusual states and responses born from topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, sublattice interference effects at saddle points such as unconventional superconductivity, orbital antiferromagnetism and flux phases, amplified anomalous Hall effects, and electronic nematic states. This review examines the theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, with the aim of elucidating fundamental mechanisms underlying the observed exotic phenomena.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015002] Published Thu Feb 12, 2026.
tldr: A review of kagome metals, focusing on exotic electronic states arising from frustrated lattice geometry.
motivation: To understand the fundamental mechanisms behind unusual phenomena in kagome metals, such as unconventional superconductivity and topological flat bands.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental work on kagome metals, analyzing electronic structure and many-body effects.
result: Identifies key phenomena including topological flat bands, massive Dirac fermions, and sublattice interference effects.
conclusion: Kagome metals host a rich variety of exotic states due to frustration and interference, but the paper is primarily a materials science review without direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Field Theories And Quantum Methods For Stochastic Reaction-diffusion Systems
authors: Mauricio J. Del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, And Wout Merbis
abstract:
Author(s): Mauricio J. del Razo, Tommaso Lamma, and Wout Merbis

The exchange of energy and molecules in a living cell, the spread of opinions through a society, and the flow of traffic in a crowded city are very different phenomena, yet they are all examples of complex systems composed of many agents that interact with each other and exchange energy or particles with the environment. These systems can be modeled as stochastic reaction-diffusion systems. In this pedagogical review, the authors apply powerful field-theoretic methods to these systems, unifying diverse approaches under a single framework. The methods are useful for handling chemical systems but also have applications in a wide range of areas such as ecology and epidemiology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015001] Published Thu Jan 22, 2026.
tldr: A pedagogical review applying field-theoretic methods to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems, with applications in chemistry, ecology, and epidemiology.
motivation: To unify diverse approaches for modeling complex systems with many interacting agents under a single field-theoretic framework.
method: The authors review and apply field-theoretic methods, including path integrals and Doi-Peliti formalism, to stochastic reaction-diffusion systems.
result: The review demonstrates how field theories can systematically handle fluctuations and correlations in reaction-diffusion processes.
conclusion: Field-theoretic methods provide a powerful and unified tool for analyzing stochastic reaction-diffusion systems across various disciplines.

title: Spin-glass Dynamics: Experiment, Theory, And Simulation
authors: E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, And D. Yllanes
abstract:
Author(s): E. D. Dahlberg, I. González-Adalid Pemartín, E. Marinari, G. Parisi, F. Ricci-Tersenghi, V. Martin-Mayor, J. Moreno-Gordo, R. L. Orbach, I. Paga, J. J. Ruiz-Lorenzo, and D. Yllanes

This review updates the field of spin glasses with broad application to a large variety of physical systems. In particular, this review tracks the progress of experiment, theory, and large-scale simulations. It highlights the importance of their synergy, from the inception of the field to the present day, and includes future opportunities for research.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045005] Published Mon Dec 15, 2025.
tldr: A review of spin-glass dynamics covering experiment, theory, and simulation.
motivation: To provide an updated overview of spin-glass research and highlight the synergy between experimental, theoretical, and computational approaches.
method: Review of experimental techniques, theoretical models, and large-scale simulations of spin glasses.
result: Summarizes key advances in understanding spin-glass dynamics and identifies future research opportunities.
conclusion: Spin-glass research continues to be a rich field with broad applications, and interdisciplinary collaboration remains essential.

title: Kitaev Quantum Spin Liquids
authors: Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, And Hae-Young Kee
abstract:
Author(s): Yuji Matsuda, Takasada Shibauchi, and Hae-Young Kee

Frustration in spin systems can prevent ordering even at =0, creating quantum spin liquids that have been sought since Anderson’s pioneering work in 1973 and his influential 1987 paper connecting them to high-temperature superconductivity. Kitaev’s solvable spin-1/2 models on a honeycomb lattice brought renewed attention to this field, with Jackeli and Khaliullin later revealing how to engineer Kitaev interactions in real materials. This review highlights theoretical and experimental developments in Kitaev spin liquids, emphasizing leading candidate materials and their broad topological properties such as chiral edge modes. Consequently, it provides essential insights for both experimentalists and theorists working on quantum spin liquid problems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045003] Published Wed Dec 03, 2025.
tldr: A review of Kitaev quantum spin liquids, focusing on candidate materials and topological properties.
motivation: To provide an overview of theoretical and experimental progress in Kitaev spin liquids, which are a paradigmatic example of frustrated magnetism.
method: Review of theoretical models (Kitaev honeycomb model) and experimental studies on candidate materials.
result: Highlights key candidate materials and their topological properties such as chiral edge modes.
conclusion: The review offers essential insights for researchers working on quantum spin liquids.

title: Colloquium: Quantum Properties And Functionalities Of Magnetic Skyrmions
authors: Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, And Christos Panagopoulos
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Petrović, Christina Psaroudaki, Peter Fischer, Markus Garst, and Christos Panagopoulos

Skyrmions are topological field configurations that were first discussed in the context of high-energy theory. In recent years, skyrmionic spin patterns in solid-state systems have received much attention, in part for their promising application potential. This Colloquium discusses quantum-mechanical aspects of such magnetic skyrmions, both for the interactions that underlie skyrmion formation and for quantum features of the skyrmions themselves.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 031001] Published Tue Jul 08, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews quantum properties and functionalities of magnetic skyrmions, focusing on their topological nature and potential applications.
motivation: Magnetic skyrmions are promising for spintronic devices, but their quantum aspects are less explored. This review aims to consolidate quantum-mechanical understanding.
method: The paper surveys theoretical and experimental work on skyrmion formation, quantum features, and interactions, providing a comprehensive overview.
result: It highlights quantum effects such as tunneling, superposition, and entanglement in skyrmions, and discusses their potential for quantum information processing.
conclusion: Quantum skyrmions may enable new functionalities, but further research is needed to harness them for practical quantum technologies.

title: Spin-dependent Exotic Interactions
authors: Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, And Dmitry Budker
abstract:
Author(s): Lei Cong, Wei Ji, Pavel Fadeev, Filip Ficek, Min Jiang, Victor V. Flambaum, Haosen Guan, Derek F. Jackson Kimball, Mikhail G. Kozlov, Yevgeny V. Stadnik, and Dmitry Budker

This review presents a comprehensive summary of theoretical investigations and experimental searches for spin-dependent interactions beyond the standard model. These interactions may be mediated by various types of exotic bosons, and their existence and properties may, in turn, explain the nature of dark matter and dark energy. The described experiments also probe the discrete fundamental symmetries of nature.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025005] Published Tue Jun 24, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of experimental searches for spin-dependent exotic interactions beyond the standard model, probing dark matter and fundamental symmetries.
motivation: To understand the nature of dark matter and dark energy through spin-dependent forces mediated by exotic bosons.
method: Review of theoretical models and experimental techniques for detecting spin-dependent interactions.
result: Summarizes current constraints and future prospects for various exotic spin-dependent interactions.
conclusion: Spin-dependent exotic interactions remain an active area of research with potential to reveal new physics beyond the standard model.

title: Colloquium: Materials That Exceed Classical Thermodynamic Bounds On Properties
authors: Roderic S. Lakes
abstract:
Author(s): Roderic S. Lakes

Classical thermodynamic bounds provide constraints on values that are expected in measurements of certain physical properties. In a variety of fields, some measurements exceed these bounds. This apparent violation of thermodynamics arises because the measurements are made in ways that violate the underlying assumptions made when deriving these bounds. This Colloquium describes a wide variety of circumstances where such violations occur and which of the underlying assumptions are violated in each case. It also describes how interesting material properties can be developed using materials designed to violate these assumptions.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021002] Published Wed May 14, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews materials that appear to exceed classical thermodynamic bounds on properties, explaining how violations arise from assumptions not being met.
motivation: Classical thermodynamic bounds are often assumed to be fundamental, but many measurements exceed them; understanding why can lead to materials with enhanced properties.
method: The paper surveys a wide range of examples from different fields, analyzing which underlying assumptions (e.g., equilibrium, linearity) are violated in each case.
result: It identifies common mechanisms for apparent violations, such as non-equilibrium conditions, anisotropy, or hierarchical structures, and shows how these can be exploited.
conclusion: Materials can be designed to exceed classical bounds by deliberately violating the assumptions behind those bounds, opening avenues for novel material properties.

title: Colloquium: Synthetic Quantum Matter In Nonstandard Geometries
authors: Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, And Christof Weitenberg
abstract:
Author(s): Tobias Grass, Dario Bercioux, Utso Bhattacharya, Maciej Lewenstein, Hai Son Nguyen, and Christof Weitenberg

This Colloquium presents ways to implement fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems. The study of quantum many-body physics in these exotic geometries permits simulation of phenomena from topology in condensed matter to models of gravity and cosmology.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 011001] Published Tue Mar 25, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on implementing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in atomic, photonic, and electronic systems for quantum many-body physics.
motivation: To explore quantum many-body physics in nonstandard geometries, enabling simulation of phenomena from condensed matter topology to gravity and cosmology.
method: Reviews experimental and theoretical approaches for realizing fractal lattices, curved spaces, and higher dimensions in various quantum platforms.
result: Summarizes progress in synthetic quantum matter in exotic geometries, highlighting connections to topology and cosmology.
conclusion: These synthetic systems offer new avenues for studying quantum many-body physics beyond standard geometries.

title: Self-aligning Polar Active Matter
authors: Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, And Amir Shee
abstract:
Author(s): Paul Baconnier, Olivier Dauchot, Vincent Démery, Gustavo Düring, Silke Henkes, Cristián Huepe, and Amir Shee

What if active units could align–or even antialign–their orientation with their own velocity? This intriguing self-alignment property unlocks a spectrum of fascinating behaviors, from single self-propelled particles orbiting in harmonic traps to transformative collective phenomena like synchronized motion in dense or solid elastic assemblies. Unlike systems where units simply mimic their neighbors, self-alignment fundamentally reshapes how motion emerges, paving the way for groundbreaking discoveries in biology, smart materials, and robotics. This review uncovers the hidden power of self-alignment in active systems, introduces a unified mathematical and conceptual framework, explores existing models of self-alignment, and highlights its transformative impact on the study and real-world applications of active systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015007] Published Thu Mar 20, 2025.
tldr: A review of self-alignment in polar active matter, covering single-particle and collective behaviors.
motivation: To unify the understanding of self-alignment in active systems and highlight its potential for biology, smart materials, and robotics.
method: The paper reviews existing models and experiments, and proposes a unified mathematical and conceptual framework for self-alignment.
result: Self-alignment enables novel behaviors such as orbiting in harmonic traps and synchronized motion in dense assemblies.
conclusion: Self-alignment is a fundamental property that reshapes motion in active systems, with broad implications for applications.

title: Massive Quantum Systems As Interfaces Of Quantum Mechanics And Gravity
authors: Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, And Clara C. Wanjura
abstract:
Author(s): Sougato Bose, Ivette Fuentes, Andrew A. Geraci, Saba Mehsar Khan, Sofia Qvarfort, Markus Rademacher, Muddassar Rashid, Marko Toroš, Hendrik Ulbricht, and Clara C. Wanjura

The authors review theories and experimental state-of-the-art efforts to study the effects of gravity on massive quantum systems. Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force and may be addressed via precision quantum probes. Experiments testing whether the quantum nature of gravity causes decoherence and collapse of matter-wave functions and whether it can mediate entanglement between separate massive particles are underway, and their results will guide the theoretical description of gravity effects on a laboratory scale.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015003] Published Thu Feb 13, 2025.
tldr: A review of theoretical and experimental efforts to study gravity's effects on massive quantum systems, exploring whether gravity induces decoherence or entanglement.
motivation: Classical gravity is the least precisely tested natural force, and quantum probes may reveal its quantum nature.
method: The paper reviews theories of gravity-induced decoherence and collapse, and experiments testing gravity-mediated entanglement between massive particles.
result: Ongoing experiments aim to determine whether gravity causes decoherence or can mediate entanglement, guiding future theoretical descriptions.
conclusion: Massive quantum systems serve as interfaces to probe quantum gravity effects, but conclusive results are pending.

title: Superluminal Transformations And Indeterminism
authors: Amrapali Sen And Flavio Del Santo
abstract: Quantum theory is widely regarded as fundamentally indeterministic, yet classical frameworks can also exhibit indeterminism once infinite information is abandoned. At the same time, relativity is usually taken to forbid superluminal signalling, although Lorentz symmetry formally admits superluminal transformations (SpTs). Dragan and Ekert have argued that SpTs entail a form of indeterminism analogous to that encountered in quantum theory. Here, we derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from a set of natural assumptions: any framework admitting non-order-preserving SpTs must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon the notion that time determines a preferred causal ordering. In particular, one possible implication is that any theory accommodating SpTs suggests an ontology with unbounded informational content, akin to deterministic classical theories formulated over the real numbers. Consequently, any ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information.
tldr: The paper explores the connection between superluminal transformations and indeterminism, deriving a no-go theorem that challenges the idea that finite information can account for quantum-like indeterminacy.
motivation: To understand whether superluminal transformations can naturally lead to indeterminism analogous to quantum theory, and to identify the necessary assumptions for such a framework.
method: The authors derive a theory-independent no-go theorem from a set of natural assumptions about information, time symmetry, memory, and causal ordering.
result: Any theory admitting non-order-preserving superluminal transformations must either abandon finite information, relinquish time-symmetric informational content, deny that the past stores memory, or abandon time-determined causal ordering.
conclusion: Ontic indeterminacy associated with superluminal transformations cannot originate from finite information, suggesting that such indeterminism would require unbounded informational content.

title: Wave Packet Motion In A Quantized Electromagnetic Field: Analytic Results
authors: Szabolcs Hack, Béla Gábor Pusztai, Krisztina Joós, Sándor Varró, Attila Czirják And Péter Földi
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of a charged particle interacting with a multimode quantized electromagnetic field and obtain an analytic solution for the full electron-field system. In the present finite-mode formulation the total electron-field dynamics remains closed and unitary. The framework enables the calculation of position expectation values and uncertainties for arbitrary wave packets and field states, allowing us to identify quantum corrections to the corresponding classical motion. While the corrections to the position expectation value are weak and largely insensitive to the quantum state of the field, the wave packet broadening exhibits a pronounced dependence on the field state. In particular, the quantum uncertainty of the radiation is directly imprinted onto the spatial uncertainty of the particle. We illustrate these effects for Gaussian wave packets interacting with coherent, Fock, and squeezed states, including bright squeezed vacuum. The interaction with a finite-duration laser pulse is also analyzed as a multimode example. Our results provide a transparent analytic route toward understanding how quantum fluctuations of light influence electron dynamics in strong-field settings.
tldr: Analytic solution for charged particle dynamics in a quantized electromagnetic field, showing quantum corrections to classical motion.
motivation: To understand how quantum fluctuations of light affect electron dynamics in strong-field settings, providing analytic insights beyond numerical simulations.
method: Finite-mode formulation of the full electron-field system, solving the Schrödinger equation analytically for arbitrary wave packets and field states.
result: Quantum corrections to position expectation are weak and insensitive to field state, but wave packet broadening strongly depends on field state, directly imprinting field uncertainty onto particle spatial uncertainty.
conclusion: The analytic framework reveals transparent connections between quantum field fluctuations and electron dynamics, useful for strong-field physics and quantum optics.

title: Cavity-induced Multispin Interactions And Phase Transitions In Ultracold Fermi Gases
authors: Shi-Liang Zhu And Z D Wang Zhen Zheng
abstract: The many-body physics of higher-spin systems is expected to host qualitatively new matter phases, but realizing them requires the controllable interactions between multispin components that can be tuned independently for each component. Here we propose a scheme that meets this demand in ultracold Fermi gases. By engineering the atom-cavity coupling, we generate cavity-induced effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. Focusing on the simplest spin-1 case, we obtain two independent scattering channels whose relative strengths and signs are determined by the Clebsch–Gordan coefficients and optical-field parameters. The resulting Hamiltonian combines the on-site Cooper pairing with the off-site repulsion, and drives a continuous transition from the superfluid to the spin-density-wave phase. The coexistence region is reminiscent of a supersolid, yet the self-organized modulation appears in the spin density profile of a higher-spin representation, rather than in the number density profile. The proposal can be implemented with the existing techniques in ultracold atoms. Therefore it offers a versatile platform for quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate cavity-induced multispin interactions in ultracold Fermi gases, enabling quantum simulation of higher-spin many-body physics and phase transitions.
motivation: Higher-spin systems can host novel quantum phases, but realizing controllable multispin interactions is challenging. The authors aim to engineer such interactions using cavity-mediated couplings.
method: By coupling ultracold Fermi gases to an optical cavity, they induce effective interactions between pseudo-spin states via multiple Raman and cavity paths. For spin-1, they obtain two independent scattering channels with tunable strengths.
result: The resulting Hamiltonian drives a continuous transition from superfluid to spin-density-wave phase, with a coexistence region reminiscent of supersolid order in spin density.
conclusion: The scheme is experimentally feasible with existing techniques and provides a versatile platform for simulating higher-spin many-body physics.

title: Observation Of Alignment Tensor Effects In Metastability-exchange Collisions With Highly Polarized 3 ...
authors: Yida Sha, Kaiwen Yi, Xingqing Jin, Matteo Fadel And Xiang Peng
abstract: Highly polarized ensembles prepared by metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) have been widely used in precision measurements and fundamental physics. Metastability-exchange (ME) collisions, serving as the basis of MEOP, are traditionally described in terms of atomic orientation, while the significant contributions of metastable alignment tensor at high polarization remain unexplored. In this work, we develop a linearized model under mean-field approximation to investigate alignment tensor effects in highly polarized , which originate from the metastable manifold and are revealed through ME-induced relaxation and frequency shift. By means of free-induction-decay measurements, a pronounced dependence on nuclear polarization is experimentally observed in the response of the ground-state-metastable hybrid ensembles to the external magnetic field. Furthermore, after obtaining the characteristics of tensor-induced phenomena, we demonstrate good agreement between the experiment and the theory. This work advances the understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized using MEOP. It further provides applications in systematic error correction of high-accuracy magnetometry, as well as in optimal protocol for the generation of nuclear spin-squeezed states.
tldr: This paper studies alignment tensor effects in metastability-exchange collisions with highly polarized 3He, focusing on nuclear spin dynamics and magnetometry applications.
motivation: To understand alignment tensor contributions in highly polarized 3He ensembles, which are not captured by traditional orientation-based models, and to improve precision measurements.
method: Develops a linearized mean-field model and validates it with free-induction-decay measurements on metastability-exchange optical pumping (MEOP) ensembles.
result: Observes a pronounced dependence of ground-state-metastable hybrid ensemble response on nuclear polarization, and achieves good agreement between theory and experiment.
conclusion: Advances understanding of nuclear spin dynamics in highly polarized 3He and provides applications for systematic error correction in magnetometry and generation of spin-squeezed states.

title: Exploring Exotic Spin-dependent Interactions Beyond The Standard Model: Theoretical Foundations And Experimental Investigations
authors: L Y Wu And H Yan
abstract: New interactions mediated by novel particles propose solutions to several important questions in modern physics. Axions serve as examples of such particles; they are lightweight and interact weakly with ordinary matter. This category of particles, including those similar to axions—termed axion-like particles (ALPs)—arises from diverse theoretical frameworks, such as the Peccei-Quinn mechanism addressing the strong CP problem, string theory, and spontaneous supersymmetry breaking. Given their light mass and weak coupling, ALPs are also possible candidates for cold dark matter. Introducing these new interactions mediated by novel particles not only tackles several challenges in modern physics but also raises a crucial question: Are there undiscovered interactions beyond the standard model (SM)? Many of the interactions predicted by these theories are spin-dependent, which is the primary focus of this review. In this review, we first outline the theoretical foundations for investigating exotic spin-dependent interactions, highlighting their importance in various models beyond the SM. We examine the potential roles of new lightweight particles in mediating these interactions, which may enhance our understanding of dark matter. Relevant formulas derived from theoretical models are included to support experimental investigations. Following this theoretical framework, we conduct a detailed review of recent experimental efforts to detect these exotic interactions. A systematic review of current constraints on these interactions is presented, along with an assessment of various detection approaches.
tldr: A review of exotic spin-dependent interactions beyond the Standard Model, focusing on axion-like particles and their experimental detection.
motivation: To explore new interactions mediated by novel particles that could address open questions in physics, such as dark matter and the strong CP problem.
method: The paper reviews theoretical foundations of spin-dependent interactions and systematically surveys recent experimental efforts to detect them.
result: It presents a comprehensive overview of current constraints on exotic spin-dependent interactions and various detection approaches.
conclusion: The review highlights the potential of spin-dependent interactions to reveal new physics beyond the Standard Model, but does not advance quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Observation Of Floquet Tensor Monopoles
authors: Hao Yuan, Weixuan Zhang, Na Sun And Xiangdong Zhang
abstract: Tensor monopoles, topological singularities of Kalb–Ramond tensor gauge fields, have garnered widespread attention in high-energy and condensed matter physics. They give rise to exotic phenomena such as quantized magnetoelectric responses and chiral boundary states, acting as potential building blocks for the development of topological devices in high-dimensional space. However, theoretical studies and experimental realizations reported to date have remained in static settings, and the realization of Floquet tensor monopoles (FTMs) and their associated anomalous non-equilibrium topological features has yet to be achieved.
