Here, we report the first theoretical and experimental implementation of FTMs in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system. We systematically uncover the driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of FTMs, together with their anomalous bulk-edge correspondence. These phenomena are unique to FTMs and have no static counterparts. In experiments, we design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits, and directly observe the controllable motion of FTMs in k-space and their induced 3D Fermi-arc surface states by tuning the driving frequency. Our findings extend tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime, providing a theoretical and experimental platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and laying the groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.
tldr: This paper reports the first experimental observation of Floquet tensor monopoles in a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, extending tensor monopole research to the non-equilibrium regime.
motivation: Tensor monopoles have been studied in static settings, but their realization in non-equilibrium systems and associated anomalous topological features had not been achieved.
method: The authors design and fabricate time-varying topological circuits to realize a four-dimensional non-equilibrium system, and observe the motion of Floquet tensor monopoles in k-space by tuning the driving frequency.
result: They demonstrate driving-frequency controlled creation, motion, and annihilation of Floquet tensor monopoles, along with anomalous bulk-edge correspondence and 3D Fermi-arc surface states.
conclusion: This work provides a platform for exploring exotic topological phases in dynamic tensor gauge fields and lays groundwork for functional topological devices with real-time control.

title: Pseudo-Hermitian Magnon Dynamics
authors: Xi-Guang Wang And Jamal Berakdar
abstract: A defining quantity of a physical system is its energy which is represented by the Hamiltonian. In closed quantum mechanical or/and fully coherent wave-based systems the Hamiltonian is introduced as a Hermitian operator which ensures real energy spectrum and secures the decomposition of any state over a complete basis set that spans the space where states live. Pseudo-Hermitian, or PT symmetric, systems are a special class of non-Hermitian ones. They describe open systems but may still have real energy spectrum. The eigenmodes are however not orthogonal in general. This qualitative difference to Hermitian physics has a range of consequences for the physical behavior of the system in the steady state or when it is subjected to external perturbations. This overview reviews the recent progress in the field of pseudo-Hermitian physics as it unfolds when applied to low-energy excitations of magnetically ordered materials. The focus is mainly on long wavelength spin excitations (spin waves) with magnons being the energy quanta of these excitations. Various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures with different types of coupling to the environments as well as spatio-temporally engineered systems will be discussed with a focus on the particular aspects that are brought about by the pseudo-Hermiticity such as mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric assisted Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and field-induced enhanced sensitivity.
tldr: A review of pseudo-Hermitian magnon dynamics in magnetically ordered materials, focusing on non-Hermitian effects such as mode amplification and non-reciprocal propagation.
motivation: To explore the unique physical behaviors arising from pseudo-Hermiticity in magnonic systems, which differ fundamentally from Hermitian systems.
method: The paper reviews theoretical and experimental progress in pseudo-Hermitian magnonics, covering various setups including ferromagnetic, antiferromagnetic, magnonic crystals, and hybrid structures.
result: Key phenomena discussed include mode amplification, non-reciprocal propagation, magnon cloaking, non-Hermitian skin effect, PT-symmetric Floquet engineering, topological energy transfer, and enhanced sensitivity.
conclusion: Pseudo-Hermitian magnonics offers new avenues for controlling spin waves and may lead to novel applications, but the field is still developing.

title: A Comprehensive Review On Master Stability Functions In Complex Network Dynamics
authors: Priodyuti Pradhan And Chandrakala Meena Suman Acharyya
abstract: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon observed across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. Understanding the stability of a synchronization phenomenon is crucial for ensuring functionality in various complex systems. The master stability function (MSF) framework has emerged as a powerful and elegant tool for analyzing the stability of synchronization in coupled dynamical systems. By separating the effects of the node dynamics from the network structure, the MSF offers deep insights into synchronization behavior. However, a major challenge lies in determining the MSF for complex dynamical networks driven by nonlinear interaction mechanisms. These mechanisms introduce additional complexity due to the intricate connectivity of the interacting elements and the complex dynamics governed by nonlinear processes, diverse parameters, and the higher dimensionality of the system. Although MSF analysis has been widely used for more than past 25 years, a comprehensive and systematic investigation of MSF across various networked systems is still lacking. In this article, we present a simplified and unified analysis for the MSF in various undirected and directed networked systems. We begin by formulating the MSF framework in pairwise coupled identical systems and extend our analysis to directed networks and multilayer networks, considering both intralayer and interlayer interactions. Furthermore, we analyze the MSF formalism for higher-order networks. To facilitate understanding, we complement the theoretical developments with numerical analysis of synchronization stability in coupled systems. We also propose algorithms for computing the MSF, identifying stability regimes, and classifying the MSF behaviors. Overall, the primary goal of this review is to present a systematic study of the MSF in various coupled dynamical networks in a clear and structured manner, making this powerful tool more accessible. Furthermore, we highlight underexplored areas in the application of the MSF and discuss emerging directions, such as estimating the MSF using machine learning approaches.
tldr: A comprehensive review of master stability functions for analyzing synchronization stability in complex networks, covering pairwise, directed, multilayer, and higher-order networks.
motivation: Synchronization is a fundamental emergent phenomenon in natural and engineered systems, and understanding its stability is crucial. The master stability function (MSF) framework is a powerful tool, but a systematic investigation across various networked systems is lacking.
method: The authors formulate the MSF framework for pairwise coupled identical systems, extend it to directed and multilayer networks with intralayer and interlayer interactions, and analyze higher-order networks. They complement theory with numerical analysis and propose algorithms for computing MSF and classifying stability regimes.
result: A unified and simplified MSF analysis is presented for various undirected and directed networked systems, including multilayer and higher-order networks. Algorithms for computing MSF and identifying stability regimes are provided.
conclusion: The review systematically presents MSF for various coupled dynamical networks, making the tool more accessible, and highlights underexplored areas and emerging directions such as machine learning approaches for MSF estimation.

title: ViBra: Configuration Interaction For Anharmonic Vibrational Spectroscopy And Quantum-Sampled Configuration Spaces
authors: Raphael F. Ligorio, Marco Antonio Barroca, Alan Duriez, Mathias B. Steiner
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22850v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum-centric workflows are a promising route to improving the accuracy of property predictions in computational chemistry and materials science. By integrating quantum sampling algorithms with classical solvers, electronic structure calculations have recently demonstrated their potential even on noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices. In principle, the method of Vibrational Configuration Interaction (VCI) is suitable for integration with quantum sampling algorithms as well. However, demonstrations of computational workflows for quantum-centric, vibrational property predictions are still lacking. Here, we introduce a methodology for performing anharmonic vibrational structure calculations that can be deployed in a hybrid, quantum-classical mode. Starting from a quartic force field, the approach combines a Vibrational Self-Consistent Field (VSCF) with VCI in either Full, Selected (S-VCI), or Symmetry-Adapted (SA-VCI) mode. In S-VCI, an Epstein-Nesbet perturbative screening significantly reduces the configuration space while retaining high predictive accuracy. A state-list input enables the integration of externally generated vibrational configurations as a seed space. As a proof-of-concept, we demonstrate a hybrid, quantum-classical computational workflow, in which a quantum sampling algorithm provides the seed. Our vibrational wave function analysis package ViBra, equipped with a graphical interface, is available at [URL].
tldr: This paper introduces a hybrid quantum-classical workflow for anharmonic vibrational structure calculations using configuration interaction, but it is focused on computational chemistry rather than quantum information theory or thermodynamics.
motivation: To improve accuracy of vibrational property predictions in computational chemistry by integrating quantum sampling algorithms with classical vibrational configuration interaction methods.
method: Combines Vibrational Self-Consistent Field (VSCF) with Full, Selected, or Symmetry-Adapted Vibrational Configuration Interaction (VCI), using Epstein-Nesbet perturbative screening to reduce configuration space and a state-list input for externally generated configurations from quantum sampling.
result: Demonstrates a proof-of-concept hybrid quantum-classical workflow where a quantum sampling algorithm provides the seed configuration space for VCI.
conclusion: The methodology enables anharmonic vibrational structure calculations in a hybrid mode, but the contribution is primarily to computational chemistry, not to the user's research directions.

title: Quantum Fluctuation-driven Transport Crossover Between Two Liquid States In Distinguishable Helium-4
authors: Mika Tanabe, Momoko Tsujimoto, Kenichi Kinugawa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23127v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show the emergence of a quantum fluctuation-driven transport crossover between two liquid states in distinguishable helium-4 obeying Boltzmann statistics, in the absence of atomic exchange. Using path integral centroid molecular dynamics simulations over 0.1-3.3 K and 1-60 bar, we investigate the transport properties of two distinct liquid states: the low quantum-dispersion liquid (LQDL) and the high quantum-dispersion liquid (HQDL). While LQDL exhibits conventional liquid behavior consistent with the Stokes-Einstein (SE) relation, HQDL emerges at lower temperatures and displays anomalous gas-like transport characterized by superdiffusion and ultralow viscosity, accompanied by a breakdown of the SE relation. This counterintuitive emergence of gas-like dynamics upon cooling reflects the dominant role of nuclear quantum fluctuations, in contrast to thermal fluctuations at higher temperatures. Across the LQDL-HQDL boundary, we identify a transport crossover marked by a qualitative change in the velocity autocorrelation function (VAF), a transition in the Prandtl number, and the emergence of transport minima in shear and kinematic viscosities, thermal conductivity, and thermal diffusivity. These minima reflect a crossover from liquid-like to gas-like transport upon cooling in the low-temperature subcritical region, in addition to the universal transport minima observed in the supercritical regime. The transition from oscillatory to monotonic VAF defines a second Frenkel line, distinct from the conventional Frenkel line observed in the supercritical region. LQDL is a heat-transport-dominated dissipative fluid, whereas HQDL is a momentum-dominated inertial fluid. These results demonstrate that nuclear quantum fluctuations alone induce gas-like liquid behavior and provide a unified picture of transport phenomena in distinguishable helium-4 without superfluidity.
tldr: This paper studies transport crossover in distinguishable helium-4 driven by nuclear quantum fluctuations, without superfluidity.
motivation: To understand how quantum fluctuations alone can induce gas-like transport in a liquid upon cooling, challenging classical expectations.
method: Path integral centroid molecular dynamics simulations over a range of temperatures and pressures.
result: Identifies a low quantum-dispersion liquid (LQDL) and a high quantum-dispersion liquid (HQDL) with anomalous gas-like transport, including superdiffusion and ultralow viscosity.
conclusion: Nuclear quantum fluctuations can produce gas-like liquid behavior and a transport crossover, providing a unified picture without superfluidity.

title: Individual And Collective Gains From Cooperation And Reciprocity In A Dynamic-network Prisoner's Dilemma Driven By Extraversion, Openness, And Agreeableness
authors: David Abi\'an, Jorge Bernad, Sergio Ilarri, Raquel Trillo-Lado
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23168v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: How do stable personality differences shape cooperation when social ties can form and dissolve? We model a repeated Prisoner's Dilemma on an endogenous network in which three continuous Big Five traits map to transparent local mechanisms: Extraversion sets a target number of partners, Openness determines how broadly agents search beyond friends-of-friends, and Agreeableness sets a baseline willingness to cooperate. At each encounter, agents combine this baseline with the partner's directly observed history; there are no trait labels, gossip, or global reputations. Ties form when agents are under-connected and are cut when they become over-connected, with cuts prioritising partners who have defected more often. We vary network size (N=30--200), population composition, and the balance between trait-driven and history-driven behaviour. Three robust patterns emerge. First, cooperate first, then reciprocate---high initial willingness to cooperate combined with history-sensitive response---produces systems that are simultaneously more prosperous, fairer, and safer. Second, personality has predictable conditional effects: Agreeableness helps when history matters but hurts when behaviour is mostly trait-driven; Extraversion amplifies the environment; Openness has little net payoff effect. Third, the network reorganises accordingly: degree assortativity stays near zero, whereas agreeable agents increasingly connect to one another when cooperation takes hold.
tldr: This paper studies cooperation in a dynamic-network Prisoner's Dilemma driven by Big Five personality traits, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand how stable personality differences shape cooperation when social ties can form and dissolve.
method: Agent-based model with continuous Big Five traits mapping to local mechanisms: extraversion sets target partners, openness determines search breadth, agreeableness sets baseline cooperation; ties form/cut based on connectivity and defection history.
result: Three patterns: cooperate-first-then-reciprocate yields prosperity, fairness, safety; personality effects are conditional; network reorganizes with agreeable agents connecting when cooperation takes hold.
conclusion: Personality traits have predictable effects on cooperation in dynamic networks, with implications for social dynamics.

title: Chiral Dynamics Of An Intruder Across Dilute And Hydrodynamic Regimes
authors: Ignacio Pagonabarraga Rapha\"el Maire
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and simulate an analytically tractable model for an intruder of arbitrary shape in a nonequilibrium bath, with chirality originating from the bath, the intruder, or their coupling. In the dilute regime, a Langevin description derived from a Boltzmann-Lorentz equation shows how intruder geometry governs ratchet effects and odd response. In the dense regime, the dynamics of the intruder are instead governed by the hydrodynamic modes of the bath and edge currents, which are described by a Stokes equation including a chiral torque density. Our results link shape to chiral transport and show that odd response arises from distinct mechanisms in the dilute and dense limits.
tldr: A model for chiral dynamics of an intruder in a nonequilibrium bath, linking shape to odd transport in dilute and dense regimes.
motivation: To understand how chirality and shape affect transport in active matter systems, bridging dilute and hydrodynamic regimes.
method: Analytical Langevin description from Boltzmann-Lorentz equation for dilute regime; Stokes equation with chiral torque density for dense regime; numerical simulations.
result: Intruder geometry governs ratchet effects and odd response; distinct mechanisms in dilute vs dense limits.
conclusion: Shape is a key control parameter for chiral transport in active baths, with potential applications in microrheology and active matter.

title: Nested Integral Generator Theorem: From Operator Tautologies To Families Of Exact Integral Identities
authors: Ghasem Asadi Cordshooli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inserting resolutions of the identity is a standard technique for representing states and operators throughout quantum theory, quantum field theory, and related areas of mathematical physics. This paper elevates this procedure to a rigorous, representation-independent framework through the Nested Integral Generator Theorem. Starting from operator tautologies, the theorem systematically generates exact multi-fold integral identities by successive insertions of continuous resolutions of the identity followed by projection onto arbitrary orthonormal basis vectors. The resulting construction applies to arbitrary finite compositions of closed operators acting on arbitrary target states and establishes a general mapping from operator equalities to families of exact integral identities. Using the theory of vector-valued integration, explicit and verifiable sufficient conditions are derived under which inner products may be interchanged rigorously with Bochner integrals, thereby placing a step that is often left implicit in the physics literature on a firm mathematical foundation. As an immediate consequence, the theorem yields exact integral representations for individual operator functions. Its scope is illustrated through elementary, polynomial, and analytic single-mode operators, as well as single- and two-mode Gaussian unitaries, including squeezing and beam splitting. The framework is further applied to two nontrivial examples beyond standard Gaussian calculations: an exact integral representation of a Kerr-squeezed coherent-state overlap and exact Fock-basis matrix elements for a composite two-mode Gaussian network expressed in terms of bivariate Hermite polynomials.
tldr: The paper presents a rigorous mathematical framework for generating exact integral identities from operator tautologies using nested resolutions of the identity.
motivation: To provide a representation-independent and mathematically rigorous foundation for a common technique in quantum theory and mathematical physics.
method: The Nested Integral Generator Theorem is developed using vector-valued integration and Bochner integrals to justify interchange of inner products with integrals.
result: Exact integral representations are derived for operator functions, including Gaussian unitaries and a Kerr-squeezed coherent-state overlap.
conclusion: The framework offers a systematic way to generate exact integral identities, but its contribution is primarily mathematical rather than advancing specific quantum information or thermodynamics directions.

title: Can Second-Order Nonlinearity In Metal-Dielectric Metamaterials Pave A Way Toward Elusive Photonic Time Crystals?
authors: Jacob B Khurgin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While a tremendous amount of theoretical work has been dedicated to time-varying photonics, practical implementation in the optical range has relied almost exclusively on transparent conductive oxides , which remain severely constrained by being slow and highly lossy. To bypass these limitations, I propose an alternative platform utilizing ultrafast second-order nonlinearities within an epsilon-near-zero semiconductor-silver metamaterial. Due to the relatively low loss in silver and polarization-selective pumping, ultra-low pump absorption prevents thermal degradation, while absorption of the probe is sufficiently low to simultaneously permit the multi-cycle interaction lengths necessary for signal detection. I find that with pump powers of 100s of GW/cm2 one can open a wide momentum bandgap of tens of percents and achieve net parametric gain in time, offering a robust pathway to realizing photonic time crystals in optical range.
tldr: Proposes using second-order nonlinearity in metal-dielectric metamaterials to realize photonic time crystals in the optical range.
motivation: Current time-varying photonics platforms are slow and lossy; this work aims to bypass those limitations.
method: Theoretical analysis of an epsilon-near-zero semiconductor-silver metamaterial with ultrafast second-order nonlinearities and polarization-selective pumping.
result: With pump powers of hundreds of GW/cm², a wide momentum bandgap of tens of percent and net parametric gain in time can be achieved.
conclusion: The proposed platform offers a robust pathway to realizing photonic time crystals in the optical range.

title: Multi-Path Routing In Decentralized Exchange Networks: Convex Allocation And An Improving-Path Certificate
authors: Ilia Zhavoronkov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22540v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a graph-theoretic and convex optimization framework for multi-path routing in decentralized exchange networks, together with its implementation and empirical evaluation on Ethereum mainnet. The framework models the market as a directed token multigraph whose arcs carry AMM exchange functions. Routing is decomposed into two implemented layers: candidate path generation via gas-aware marginal k-shortest-path enumeration, where edge scores embed expected execution cost directly into graph traversal with an explicit pool-simple constraint tracked during path construction, and continuous flow allocation over the selected candidates solved as a concave maximization over a simplex with a per-pool price-impact cap. Under standard concavity and monotonicity assumptions, the KKT conditions imply marginal-output equalization across active paths. The central technical contribution is an improving-path certificate: after solving the allocation on k=20 candidate paths, the KKT multiplier is used as a threshold to determine via a single shortest-path query whether any omitted pool-simple path could improve the current solution; in our implementation the certificate confirms sufficiency in the majority of epochs. Execution is protected by an on-chain slippage tolerance enforced at the smart-contract level. We evaluate the implemented engine against four production DEX aggregators on repeated WETH-USDT quote observations across six trade sizes on Ethereum mainnet: median shortfall is below 5 bps across all sizes and top-3 quote rank exceeds 57% of epochs.
tldr: This paper presents a convex optimization framework for multi-path routing in decentralized exchange networks, focusing on gas-aware path enumeration and flow allocation with an improving-path certificate.
motivation: Decentralized exchange aggregators need efficient multi-path routing to minimize slippage and gas costs, but existing solutions lack formal guarantees on solution quality.
method: The framework models the market as a directed token multigraph with AMM exchange functions, decomposes routing into candidate path generation via gas-aware k-shortest-path enumeration and continuous flow allocation via concave maximization, and uses KKT conditions to derive an improving-path certificate.
result: Empirical evaluation on Ethereum mainnet shows median shortfall below 5 bps across six trade sizes and top-3 quote rank exceeding 57% of epochs compared to four production DEX aggregators.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a principled and efficient solution for multi-path routing in DEX networks, with formal optimality certificates and practical performance improvements.

title: A Formal Kinetic Theory For Zeroth-Order Newton Dynamics:Stein-Corrected Hessian Estimation And Curvature--Variance Trade-offs
authors: Shihao Ji, Mingyu Li, Zihui Song
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22567v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Zeroth-order Newton-type methods are useful when gradients and Hessians are unavailable, but they behave quite differently from first-order gradient-free methods. We develop a kinetic framework for algorithms that estimate both gradient and Hessian from black-box function values. The naive random-direction Hessian estimator turns out to be biased even on quadratics; a Gaussian--Stein correction is needed to estimate the Hessian of the Gaussian-smoothed objective. Linearizing the inverse Hessian exposes two noise channels: gradient noise preconditioned by the inverse Hessian, and Hessian noise transmitted through an inverse-Hessian sandwich. Under a noisy oracle the second channel carries the second-difference factor [MATH]. A small-mass kinetic lift links the finite-step Newton update to an underdamped phase-space model; the overdamped spatial limit yields a Lyapunov bound that exposes the curvature--variance trade-off between step size, batch sizes, smoothing radii, and regularization. Numerical experiments confirm estimator identities, the gradient and Hessian variance laws, dimension scaling, inverse-perturbation accuracy, and optimization behavior under query-budget and regularization ablations.
tldr: This paper develops a kinetic theory for zeroth-order Newton methods, focusing on Hessian estimation and curvature-variance trade-offs in black-box optimization.
motivation: Gradients and Hessians are often unavailable in black-box optimization, and existing zeroth-order methods lack a theoretical framework for understanding their behavior.
method: The authors propose a Gaussian-Stein corrected Hessian estimator, linearize the inverse Hessian to analyze noise channels, and use a kinetic lift to connect finite-step Newton updates to an underdamped phase-space model.
result: They derive Lyapunov bounds exposing curvature-variance trade-offs and confirm their theoretical findings with numerical experiments on estimator identities, variance laws, and optimization behavior.
conclusion: The work provides a formal kinetic theory for zeroth-order Newton methods, offering insights into estimator design and optimization under query budgets.

title: Rational Minimax Approximations For Matrix-Valued Functions: Existence, Optimality And Algorithms
authors: Chenkun Zhang Lei-Hong Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study rational minimax approximation for continuous complex matrix-valued functions in the Frobenius norm, where all approximant entries share a common denominator. This generalizes classical scalar rational approximation, with applications in system modeling, microwave design, and nonlinear eigenvalue problems. We first prove the existence of such matrix-valued approximants on point sets dense in themselves, extending Walsh's foundational scalar result. Next, we establish characterizations of the local and global minimax approximants by deriving primal/dual matrix-valued Kolmogorov criteria and a Ruttan-type sufficient condition for global optimality. For analytic functions on a continuum, we link continuum minimax approximation to approximation on its boundary, and finite boundary samples via the maximum norm principle. We show that Ruttan's sufficient optimality condition provides a certificate under which a minimax approximant obtained from the boundary or from a discrete set of boundary nodes also solves the original continuum problem. Finally, for discrete approximation, we connect these conditions to a dual problem and the related dual-based numerical method m-d-Lawson: when the original minimax problem admits a solution, strong duality is equivalent to Ruttan's sufficient optimality condition, and, the optimality equations underlying the m-d-Lawson iteration coincide with Kolmogorov's dual criteria. These results provide a theoretical basis for certifying and computing matrix-valued rational minimax approximants.
tldr: This paper studies rational minimax approximation for matrix-valued functions, extending classical scalar results to the matrix case with applications in system modeling and microwave design.
motivation: Rational minimax approximation is important in various engineering fields, but the matrix-valued case lacks theoretical foundations and algorithms.
method: The authors prove existence of matrix-valued minimax approximants on dense point sets, derive Kolmogorov criteria and Ruttan-type optimality conditions, and connect discrete and continuum approximation via maximum norm principle.
result: They establish existence, local/global optimality characterizations, and a dual-based numerical method (m-d-Lawson) with strong duality equivalence.
conclusion: The work provides a theoretical basis for certifying and computing matrix-valued rational minimax approximants.

title: Modulus Of Conically Averaged Mappings And Its Applications To Angles Between Two Subspaces
authors: Honglin Luo, Shuang Song, Xianfu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conically averaged mappings, a generalization of averaged mappings, are important in a wide range of Optimization Algorithms. In this paper, we propose the modulus of conical averagedness to classify conical averaged mappings. Introducing the monotone and comonotone values of generalized monotone mappings, we investigate their connections to the modulus of conical averagedness. In the linear setting, we completely characterize conically averaged matrices, and derive explicit and pleasing formulae for computing their modulus of averagedness. As applications, we compute the Dixmier and Friedrichs angles between two subspaces. Nonlinear results are established as extensions of the linear case. Conical averagedness of proximal and reflection mappings of hypoconvex functions are also studied.
tldr: This paper studies conically averaged mappings and their modulus, with applications to angles between subspaces, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To classify conically averaged mappings and compute their modulus, and to apply these results to compute Dixmier and Friedrichs angles between subspaces.
method: Introduces the modulus of conical averagedness, characterizes conically averaged matrices in the linear case, and extends results to nonlinear settings including proximal and reflection mappings of hypoconvex functions.
result: Derives explicit formulas for the modulus of conically averaged matrices and applies them to compute angles between subspaces.
conclusion: The work provides a complete characterization of conically averaged matrices and demonstrates applications in subspace angle computation, but is purely mathematical with no quantum or thermodynamic relevance.

title: Generalized Fine-Tuning Of Diffusion Models Via Stochastic Control And FBSDEs
authors: Lu Wang Zirui Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22660v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a generalized fine-tuning framework for diffusion models from the perspective of stochastic control. Beyond entropy-regularized formulations, we introduce a general running cost that induces a relative generalized path cost, encompassing both Kullback-Leibler divergence and optimal transport metrics as special cases. This leads to a fully nonlinear Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation. We characterize the value function through a forward-backward stochastic differential equation system and establish existence and uniqueness under standard regularity conditions. The optimal control admits a nonlinear feedback form driven by the backward stochastic differential equation gradient component. Finally, we show that generalized fine-tuning naturally introduces an additional gradient-dependent penalty, providing a unified framework for diffusion fine-tuning under general distributional constraints.
tldr: This paper proposes a generalized fine-tuning framework for diffusion models using stochastic control and forward-backward SDEs.
motivation: Existing fine-tuning methods for diffusion models are limited to specific cost functions; a unified framework is needed.
method: The authors formulate fine-tuning as a stochastic control problem with a general running cost, leading to a nonlinear HJB equation, and characterize the value function via FBSDEs.
result: The optimal control has a nonlinear feedback form with a gradient-dependent penalty, unifying KL divergence and optimal transport metrics.
conclusion: The framework provides a flexible and theoretically grounded approach for fine-tuning diffusion models under general distributional constraints.

title: Operations On Binary Linear Codes And Their Associated Graphs
authors: John H. Castillo, Lisbeth D. Delgado-Ordo\~nez, Alexander Holgu\'in-Villa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This manuscript addresses a connection between operations in coding theory and graph theory, as well as some operations in both areas. The concept of the Hasse diagram of a binary linear code, [MATH], is recall; this concept visually represents the cosets of a binary linear code with a partial ordering. The main objetive is to give a characterization of the graphs corresponding to: extended codes, punctured codes, and the direct sum of two codes, using the graph of the given binary linear code as a starting point. Relationships are established between the graphs of code operations and particular operations of graphs.
tldr: This paper explores connections between operations on binary linear codes and their associated Hasse diagrams, focusing on extended codes, punctured codes, and direct sums.
motivation: To characterize the graphs corresponding to code operations using the graph of the original binary linear code.
method: The authors recall the concept of Hasse diagrams for binary linear codes and establish relationships between code operations (extension, puncturing, direct sum) and graph operations.
result: They provide a characterization of the graphs for extended, punctured, and direct sum codes in terms of the original code's graph.
conclusion: The work establishes formal connections between coding theory and graph theory operations, but does not directly contribute to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.

title: Structured Coordination Games On Planar Graphs: A Dual Approach
authors: John S. Mcalister
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Finding Nash equilibria in the pure coordination game is trivial when every player interacts with every other player evenly. However, when players have a relational structure, the question becomes harder to answer. Here, we show that Nash equilibria to the structured coordination game represent a local notion of the Min-cut partition by way of the potential function. Using the standard relationship between partitions and subgraphs in the planar dual, we define a quasimetric space for which Nash equilibria are local minimizers of a global objective. When the game is restricted to only two strategies, these results allow us to construct a dynamic subgraph process which recapitulates the Myopic Best Response dynamics of the coordination game.
tldr: This paper studies Nash equilibria in structured coordination games on planar graphs using a dual graph approach.
motivation: Finding Nash equilibria in coordination games with relational structure is nontrivial, and the paper aims to characterize them via graph-theoretic methods.
method: The authors show that Nash equilibria correspond to local Min-cut partitions via the potential function, and use planar duality to define a quasimetric space where equilibria are local minimizers.
result: For two-strategy games, they construct a dynamic subgraph process that recapitulates Myopic Best Response dynamics.
conclusion: The work provides a novel connection between game theory and graph cuts, but does not address quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Shapley Meets Tutte
authors: Martin Loebl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We initiate the study of cooperative games where there exist groups of pre-aligned agent. For example, in a road network, the agents are cross-roads and pre-aligned groups are road-segments. For a set of datasets, the agents are attributes and each database which connects two (or more) attributes is pre-aligned. In this paper, each pre-aligned group has size two. Our goal is to find a way to determine the contribution of each individual local connection (pre-aligned couple) to the connectivity of the network, having an adversarial attack in mind or planning a defense of the network, or wanting to split the profits of the network between various owners of the individual local connections of the network. We model these contributions by Shapley values of the connectivity augmented 'local values' which are characteristic functions determined, e.g., by failure probabilities of local connections. We link the concepts of potential and Shapley values of these connectivity augmented local values to the world of chromatic and Tutte polynomials and the partition function of the Potts model from statistical physics.
tldr: This paper uses cooperative game theory and Shapley values to analyze network connectivity contributions, linking to chromatic and Tutte polynomials and the Potts model.
motivation: To determine the contribution of individual local connections to network connectivity for adversarial attack or defense planning, or profit splitting.
method: Models contributions via Shapley values of connectivity augmented 'local values' and links them to chromatic and Tutte polynomials and the Potts model partition function.
result: Establishes a connection between Shapley values and graph polynomials, enabling analysis of network connectivity contributions.
conclusion: The approach provides a way to quantify the importance of local connections in networks, with potential applications in network security and economics.

title: Multi-User Diversity Scaling In Heavy-Tailed Fading
authors: Yonathan Murin, Ali \"{o}zer Ercan, Nariman Farsad
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23135v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical multi-user diversity theory predicts that throughput over Rayleigh fading channels grows as [MATH]. In this work, we demonstrate a fundamental shift in this scaling law under heavy-tailed composite fading. Specifically, under Fisher--Snedecor [MATH] composite fading, the channel power acquires a regularly varying upper tail, shifting extreme-value statistics from the Gumbel to the Fr\'echet domain. We prove that the maximum SINR among [MATH] users scales polynomially as [MATH], where [MATH] is the shadowing severity parameter, leading to an ergodic capacity scaling of [MATH]. Crucially, this scaling persists in interference-limited Poisson networks, where aggregate co-channel interference alters the scaling constant but not the exponent. This polynomial gain is most relevant in severe-to-moderate shadowing ([MATH]), as encountered in body-area networks, vehicular/industrial IoT, and dense indoor environments, where Fr\'echet asymptotics overtake industry-standard lognormal models at practical user counts. Finally, we establish the conditions necessary to harvest this gain (showing that proportional-fair scheduling under quasi-static shadowing reverts to Gumbel scaling) and validate all analytical findings through Monte Carlo simulations, including MIMO random beamforming.
tldr: This paper studies multi-user diversity scaling in heavy-tailed fading channels, showing polynomial capacity gains under Fisher-Snedecor composite fading.
motivation: Classical multi-user diversity theory assumes Rayleigh fading, but real-world channels often exhibit heavy-tailed behavior. The authors aim to characterize throughput scaling under such conditions.
method: The authors analyze extreme-value statistics of Fisher-Snedecor composite fading, derive scaling laws for maximum SINR and ergodic capacity, and validate via Monte Carlo simulations including MIMO random beamforming.
result: Under heavy-tailed fading, the maximum SINR scales polynomially with the number of users, leading to ergodic capacity scaling as a power law, which persists in interference-limited Poisson networks.
conclusion: Heavy-tailed fading can provide significant multi-user diversity gains in severe-to-moderate shadowing environments, but proportional-fair scheduling under quasi-static shadowing reverts to classical Gumbel scaling.

title: TroPUF: Evaluating Hardware Trojan Insertion In Delay-Based Physical Unclonable Functions
authors: Amin Rezaei Marissa Marcarelli
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23418v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Delay-based Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) are commonly used for device authentication and key generation due to the fact that they rely on manufacturing induced delay variations. However, these same variations make PUFs inherently non-deterministic, which can allow malicious logic to blend in with normal circuit behavior. As a result, the act of embedding hardware Trojans directly inside the PUF primitive presents a unique security risk that is not yet well understood. This work presents a unified simulation framework for evaluating stealthy hardware Trojan insertion across multiple delay-based PUF architectures and Trojan types. Functional metrics, hardware overhead, and resistance to machine learning modeling are assessed in parallel. Results show that dormant Trojans preserve expected PUF behavior, structural characteristics, and modeling resistance. Detectable degradation appears only after activation, indicating that conventional validation techniques fail to identify embedded Trojans prior to payload execution. These findings expose a gap in current PUF security assumptions, and highlight the need to evaluate PUFs and hardware Trojans as a coupled security problem.
tldr: This paper evaluates hardware Trojan insertion in delay-based PUFs, focusing on security risks in hardware authentication.
motivation: Delay-based PUFs are used for device authentication but are vulnerable to hardware Trojans that blend with natural variations; current validation techniques fail to detect dormant Trojans.
method: A unified simulation framework assesses Trojan insertion across multiple PUF architectures and Trojan types, measuring functional metrics, hardware overhead, and machine learning resistance.
result: Dormant Trojans preserve expected PUF behavior and modeling resistance; degradation appears only after activation, exposing a gap in security assumptions.
conclusion: PUFs and hardware Trojans must be evaluated as a coupled security problem, as conventional validation fails to detect embedded Trojans before payload execution.

title: Optimality Of Bang-Bang Switching For Breaking The Chu Limit Via Time-Modulated Matching
authors: Miguel Rodrigo Castellanos Mohamed Akrout
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23688v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper shows that surpassing the Chu limit on [MATH]-factors via time-modulated matching requires non-smooth switching strategies. We derive a nonlinear differential condition to show that differentiable modulation functions are sub-optimal, then show that the optimal switching trajectory for maximizing the violation of the Chu limit is a piecewise-constant (Bang-Bang) profile. Finally, we establish an upper-bound connecting the antenna size, switching speed, and bit error rate, which reveals that switching time becomes longer as antennas become electrically smaller.
tldr: This paper proves that surpassing the Chu limit on antenna Q-factors via time-modulated matching requires non-smooth bang-bang switching, and establishes an upper bound linking antenna size, switching speed, and bit error rate.
motivation: The Chu limit imposes a fundamental bound on the Q-factor of electrically small antennas. Time-modulated matching has been proposed to break this limit, but the optimal switching strategy was unknown.
method: The authors derive a nonlinear differential condition to show differentiable modulation is sub-optimal, then prove that the optimal trajectory is a piecewise-constant (bang-bang) profile. They also derive an upper bound connecting antenna size, switching speed, and bit error rate.
result: Bang-bang switching is optimal for maximizing violation of the Chu limit, and switching time increases as antennas become electrically smaller.
conclusion: Non-smooth switching is necessary to break the Chu limit, and the results provide design guidelines for time-modulated matching networks.

result: The methodology successfully eliminates artificial reflections, yielding more accurate resonance energies.

Scanning probe techniques have transformed our ability to study materials at the atomic scale, providing atom-by-atom views of surfaces. Tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy combines scanning probes with optical fluorescence. Such optical techniques normally have spatial resolution limited by the wavelength of the light used. However, using the scanning tip itself as a nanoscale optical antenna confines the electromagnetic field to the tip apex, achieving superresolution down to the atomic scale. Fluorescence is a fundamental probe of materials that reveals electronic structure and vibronic properties by exciting electrons to higher levels and observing the photons emitted when they relax. These capabilities are of particular interest for studying and identifying molecules, submolecular structures, and their reactions. This review discusses the techniques of tip-enhanced molecular fluorescence microscopy and the new insights they have revealed.

conclusion: Tip-enhanced fluorescence microscopy provides a powerful tool for nanoscale optical characterization of molecules and surfaces.

title: On The Significance Of Wigner’s Friend In Contexts Beyond Quantum Foundations
authors: Caroline L. Jones And Markus P. Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2147 (2026).

There has been a surge of recent interest in the Wigner's Friend paradox, sparking several novel thought experiments and no-go theorems. The main narrative has been that Wigner's Friend highlights a counterintuitive feature that is unique to quantum theory, and which is closely related to the quantum measurement problem. Here, we challenge this view. We argue that the gist of the Wigner's Friend paradox can be reproduced without assuming quantum physics, and that it underlies a much broader class of enigmas in the foundations of physics and philosophy. To show this, we first consider several recently proposed Extended Wigner's Friend scenarios, and demonstrate that some of their implications for the absoluteness of observations can be reproduced by classical thought experiments that involve the duplication of agents. Crucially, some of these classical scenarios are technologically much easier to implement than their quantum counterparts. Then, we argue that the essential structural ingredient of all these scenarios is a feature that we call "Restriction A": that a physical theory cannot give us a probabilistic description of the observations of all agents. Finally, we argue that this difficulty is at the core of other puzzles in the foundations of physics and philosophy, and demonstrate this explicitly for cosmology's Boltzmann brain problem. Our analysis suggests that Wigner's Friend should be studied in a larger context, addressing a frontier of human knowledge beyond quantum foundations: to obtain reliable predictions for experiments in which these predictions can be privately but not intersubjectively verified.

.
tldr: The paper argues that the Wigner's Friend paradox is not unique to quantum theory but can be reproduced classically, and relates it to broader foundational puzzles like the Boltzmann brain problem.
motivation: To challenge the view that Wigner's Friend highlights a uniquely quantum feature and to show its relevance to other areas of physics and philosophy.
method: The authors construct classical thought experiments that mimic extended Wigner's Friend scenarios and identify a common structural feature called 'Restriction A'.
result: Classical scenarios can reproduce some implications of Wigner's Friend, and the paradox's core is a general limitation on probabilistic descriptions of all agents' observations.
conclusion: Wigner's Friend should be studied in a broader context beyond quantum foundations, addressing issues of private versus intersubjective verification.

title: Switchable Band Alignment In 2D-perovskite/WS2 Heterostructures For Tunable Exciton Transport And Valley Polarization
authors: Yingying Chen, Zeyi Liu, Zisheng Gong, Cheng Wang, Wendian Yao, Junze Li, Ti Wang, Weibo Gao And Dehui Li
abstract: Van der Waals heterostructures integrated by two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold great potential for engineering promising exciton phenomena, particularly interlayer excitons (IXs) featuring extended lifetimes and permanent out-of-plane electric dipole moments. While electrically controllable IX emission has been extensively explored in TMD heterobilayers, reconfiguring their band alignment to achieve selected exciton states and exploit these states for novel excitonic functionalities remains an urgent challenge. Here, we demonstrate dynamic exciton control by electrically tunable band alignment transitions between type-II and type-I configurations in WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures, enabling reversible conversion between charged interlayer (IX±) and charged intralayer (X−) excitons. By tailoring these exciton states, we achieve two critical functionalities: (i) 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport via transition between delocalized IX± (ON) and confined X− (OFF) states; (ii) valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio, leveraging distinct spin-valley configurations of IX± (unpolarized) and X− (polarized). Unlike twist-angle-dependent TMD heterobilayers, this platform operates independently of stacking alignment, establishing a broadly hybrid 2D system as a practical paradigm towards programmable nanophotonic circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates electrically tunable band alignment in 2D-perovskite/WS2 heterostructures for controlling exciton transport and valley polarization.
motivation: To achieve dynamic control over exciton states and functionalities in van der Waals heterostructures, enabling programmable nanophotonic circuits.
method: The authors fabricate WS2/(iso-BA)2PbI4 heterostructures and apply an electric field to switch between type-II and type-I band alignments, converting between charged interlayer and intralayer excitons.
result: They achieve 7 μm ON/OFF control of exciton transport and valley polarization switching with a 16.3 ON/OFF ratio.
conclusion: This platform offers a twist-angle-independent approach for exciton control, establishing a practical paradigm for programmable nanophotonic circuits.

title: Non-spreading Meronic Spin Defects Around Optical Vortices
authors: Miguel A Porras And Yijie Shen Nilo Mata-Cervera
abstract: Optical vortices are singularity lines where the light field intensity vanishes and its phase is undefined. These threads of darkness are adorned by Gauss’s law as lines of pure longitudinal polarization where the polarization plane tilts and winds around. The resulting spin field is as a unique structure with both features of topological texture and defect, as it includes a point defect of undefined spin enclosed by a meronic texture which spans half the spin unit sphere. This topological structure does not spread in propagation: the normalized spin field maintains a deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line while the underlying vortex beam continues to diffract. From their intrinsic nature and subwavelength confinement, these textures exhibit enhanced robustness upon isotropic perturbations such as atmospheric turbulence compared with other tailored polarization textures. Here we describe these topologies of transverse spin which decorate the phase singularity of paraxial vortex beams, highlighting the diversity of topological structures that arise in two different spaces—the spin unit sphere and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere—and discuss the underlying aspects behind their subwavelength localization.
tldr: This paper studies topological spin textures around optical vortices, focusing on meronic defects and subwavelength confinement.
motivation: To understand and characterize the unique spin structures that decorate phase singularities in paraxial vortex beams.
method: Theoretical analysis of the spin field topology using Gauss's law and the transverse-axial Poincaré sphere.
result: The normalized spin field forms a non-spreading meronic texture with deep-subwavelength confinement around the vortex line.
conclusion: These topological spin defects are robust against perturbations and may have applications in structured light and optical manipulation.

title: A Less-for-more Metamaterial Paradigm Via Laplace-Helmholtz Correspondence
authors: Zihang Guo, Fubao Yang, Tong Li, Shuihua Yang, Cheng-Wei Qiu, Jingjing He And Liujun Xu
abstract: The Laplace and Helmholtz equations dominate two fundamentally distinct physical processes: steady diffusion with a single constitutive parameter versus dynamic wave propagation with two. Manipulating complex wave dynamics through simple steady fields is typically deemed infeasible. Here, we bridge this gap by establishing the Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence, enabling a ‘less-for-more’ paradigm for metamaterial design. Rooted in a wave invariant, this framework allows the rigorous derivation of the two parameters and oscillatory field for the Helmholtz equation (the ‘more’) solely from the single parameter and steady field of the Laplace equation (the ‘less’). We demonstrate this capability by unlocking functionalities previously considered intractable, such as hyperbolic invisibility and three-dimensional freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance. We further experimentally validate our strategy via a waveguide cloak. Our results bridge static and dynamic physics, establishing a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints.
tldr: This paper establishes a mathematical correspondence between Laplace and Helmholtz equations to design metamaterials for wave manipulation using static diffusion fields.
motivation: To bridge the gap between static and dynamic physics, enabling complex wave functionalities (e.g., cloaking) through simpler steady-state design.
method: The authors derive a wave invariant that maps the single-parameter Laplace equation to the two-parameter Helmholtz equation, allowing the oscillatory field to be constructed from a steady field.
result: They demonstrate hyperbolic invisibility and 3D freeform conformal cloaking with broadband performance, and experimentally validate a waveguide cloak.
conclusion: The Laplace-Helmholtz correspondence provides a versatile gateway for manipulating waves beyond conventional constraints, but the work is focused on metamaterial design and wave physics, not quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: AI-interpreted Optical Scattering For Robust And Focal Depth-Aware Imaging
authors: Eunji Ko, Patrick Ross, Corey Hart, Wolfgang Losert
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22867v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optical scattering has conventionally been regarded as an impediment in imaging research due to the degradation of image quality during reconstruction. Nevertheless, this study explores two cases in which optical scattering may serve a beneficial role in image reconstruction tasks. We compared the No Scattering MNIST dataset with three Scattering MNIST datasets, each generated under distinct scattering conditions. To assess the information content of the resulting speckle patterns, we employed a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) approach which achieves accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art deep learning approaches, but has an interpretable latent space. We find that scattering can enhance data robustness against spatial pixel loss by effectively distributing information. We also demonstrate that scattering can enable distinctions of focal depth information. We anticipate that these findings will contribute to more efficient imaging techniques, particularly in the presence of obstacles and three-dimensional signals.
tldr: This paper explores how optical scattering can improve image reconstruction robustness and depth discrimination using a variational autoencoder.
motivation: Optical scattering is typically seen as detrimental, but the authors investigate whether it can be beneficial for distributing information and encoding focal depth.
method: They compare No Scattering MNIST with three Scattering MNIST datasets under different scattering conditions, using a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) to analyze the latent space.
result: Scattering enhances robustness against spatial pixel loss and enables distinction of focal depth information.
conclusion: Optical scattering can be leveraged for more efficient imaging in the presence of obstacles and for 3D signals.

title: Size Characterization Of Neutral Rare-gas Clusters Based On Time-resolved Polarization Anisotropy Measurements
authors: Arne Morlok, Grzegorz Kowzan, Ulrich Bangert, Yilin Li, Frank Stienkemeier, Lukas Bruder
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23064v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The size determination of neutral clusters is experimentally challenging. In particular, weakly-bound rare-gas clusters tend to fragment upon ionization, resulting in systematic errors in cluster size studies. In contrast, characterization of the temporal polarization anisotropy dephasing provides a soft detection scheme for cluster size estimation, which avoids fragmentation of the clusters. Here, we present a systematic experimental study of argon and neon clusters in the size range of 50 to 10.000 atoms using this technique. In order to extract the mean cluster sizes from the data, we present an efficient analytical model of the polarization anisotropy dephasing of an ensemble of doped clusters. The approach shows remarkable sensitivity to small changes in the mean cluster size of just a few tens of atoms and allows us to refine the widely used Hagena scaling law for the estimation of rare-gas cluster sizes.
tldr: This paper presents a method for sizing neutral rare-gas clusters using time-resolved polarization anisotropy measurements, avoiding fragmentation issues.
motivation: Accurate size determination of neutral clusters is challenging due to fragmentation upon ionization; a soft detection scheme is needed.
method: Time-resolved polarization anisotropy dephasing measurements on doped clusters are combined with an analytical model to extract mean cluster sizes.
result: The technique is sensitive to changes of a few tens of atoms and refines the Hagena scaling law for argon and neon clusters.
conclusion: Polarization anisotropy dephasing provides a reliable, non-destructive method for cluster size estimation.

title: Modelling The Correlation Structure Of Uncertain Input Parameters For Energy System Optimization
authors: Klara Maggauer, Yannick Werner, Stefan Str\"omer, Sonja Wogrin
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22630v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Statistical dependence among uncertain input parameters in stochastic energy system optimization models is often ignored, even though this can substantially bias outcomes. To address this gap, we are developing a comprehensive framework for characterizing, modelling, and benchmarking statistical dependence. In this work, we present a copula-based workflow to identify, characterize, and model linear and monotonic correlation structures between input parameters, representing the first development step towards this framework. We demonstrate our workflow using solar generation, day-ahead electricity prices, and electricity demand data in Austria between 2019 and 2025. Our results show substantial linear and monotonic dependence between these variables, and that this dependence is well captured by the copula-based approach. Finally, building on this scalable foundation, we highlight key levers for next steps towards the full framework, including time-dependent and higher-dimensional dependence modelling.
tldr: This paper develops a copula-based workflow to model statistical dependence among uncertain input parameters in energy system optimization.
motivation: Ignoring statistical dependence among uncertain inputs in energy system optimization can bias outcomes, so a framework to characterize and model such dependence is needed.
method: The authors propose a copula-based workflow to identify, characterize, and model linear and monotonic correlation structures, demonstrated on solar generation, electricity prices, and demand data from Austria.
result: Substantial linear and monotonic dependence was found among the variables, and the copula approach captured this dependence well.
conclusion: The workflow provides a scalable foundation for next steps including time-dependent and higher-dimensional dependence modeling.

title: A QUBO-Based Optimization Framework For Atm Cash Replenishment Scheduling
authors: Riccardo Aiolfi, Giulia Montani, Valeria Zaffaroni, Luca Toffanetti, Davide Veronelli, Francesca Cibrario, Davide Caputo, Davide Corbelletto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22675v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The management of cash replenishment in Automated Teller Machine (ATM) networks requires scheduling recharges in order to minimize operational costs while maintaining high service levels and avoiding cash-outs, under uncertain and time-varying withdrawal demand. This work formulates the ATM cash replenishment problem through a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model, which naturally captures nonlinear cost interactions, while incorporating operational constraints through penalty terms. The objective function combines fixed and variable replenishment costs with co-location discounts, as well as penalties for a late replenishment that could cause a service interruption. The resulting QUBO instances are solved using MegaQUBO, a GPU-accelerated QUBO solver. An empirical evaluation on a real dataset of 276 ATMs located in Italy, covering four representative months of 2022 (April, May, October, and November), benchmarks the proposed approach against a threshold-based operational policy. Results show consistent cost reductions of approximately 15%-18% while maintaining an excellent average service level (around 99.8%-99.9). Overall, the study demonstrates that QUBO-based optimization, coupled with GPU-based solving, can provide a practically deployable decision-support tool for large-scale ATM cash logistics.
tldr: This paper applies QUBO optimization to ATM cash replenishment scheduling, achieving cost reductions of 15-18%.
motivation: ATM cash replenishment scheduling is a practical logistics problem where operational costs and service levels must be balanced under uncertain demand.
method: The problem is formulated as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) model with penalty terms for constraints, solved using a GPU-accelerated solver (MegaQUBO).
result: On a real dataset of 276 ATMs, the QUBO approach reduces costs by 15-18% while maintaining service levels around 99.8-99.9%.
conclusion: QUBO-based optimization combined with GPU solving is a viable decision-support tool for large-scale ATM cash logistics.

title: Cyclotomy, External Difference Families, And Algebraic Manipulation Detection Codes
authors: Miwako Mishima Minfeng Shao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: External difference families (EDFs) are closely related to algebraic manipulation detection (AMD) codes, a cryptographic primitive that protects messages against additive tampering by an adversary who cannot observe the transmitted codeword. We first study a cyclotomic construction of external partial difference families over finite fields and derive a necessary and sufficient condition under which the resulting families are EDFs. For even block sizes up to [MATH], we obtain explicit criteria in terms of quadratic and biquadratic residues, yielding new [MATH]-optimal weak AMD codes. We then construct bounded generalized strong external difference families using cyclotomic classes over finite fields, direct products of finite fields, and generalized cyclotomic classes over integer residue rings. These constructions give infinite families of systematic [MATH]-optimal strong AMD codes with flexible parameters.
tldr: This paper constructs external difference families and algebraic manipulation detection codes using cyclotomic classes over finite fields.
motivation: To construct optimal AMD codes, which are cryptographic primitives for protecting messages against additive tampering.
method: Uses cyclotomic classes over finite fields, direct products, and generalized cyclotomic classes to construct external difference families and bounded generalized strong external difference families.
result: Derives necessary and sufficient conditions for cyclotomic constructions to be EDFs, and obtains explicit criteria for even block sizes, yielding new optimal weak and strong AMD codes.
conclusion: Provides infinite families of systematic optimal AMD codes with flexible parameters.

title: A Criterion To Determine True Minimum Distances Of Goppa Codes
authors: Shuying Dong, Hao Chen, Yaqi Chen, Ziyan Xie, Chengju Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23139v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Goppa codes play an important role in code-based cryptography due to their efficient decoding algorithms and their use as underlying private codes in the McEliece cryptosystem. To determine the true minimum distances of Goppa codes is a notoriously difficult problem. In this paper, we establish a criterion for a Goppa code to attain its designed distance. Based on this criterion, we derive a general family of Goppa codes that attain their designed distance by developing an interpolation-based construction of Goppa polynomials. We further obtain families of Goppa codes whose Goppa polynomials are determined by considering monomial, binomial, and their product of the auxiliary polynomial [MATH]. motivation: Determining the true minimum distance of Goppa codes is a notoriously difficult problem, yet crucial for assessing the security of the McEliece cryptosystem.
method: The authors derive a necessary and sufficient condition for a Goppa code to contain a codeword of weight equal to the designed distance, and use interpolation to construct Goppa polynomials that satisfy this condition.

title: Patch-fft: Unmasking Dormant Hardware Trojans With Patch-Based Frequency-Domain Transformers
authors: Amin Rezaei Hasala Senevirathne
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23421v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hardware Trojans embedded by malicious entities in integrated circuits can covertly leak sensitive information through power side channels, often remaining undetected in their dormant state until specific trigger conditions activate their malicious behavior. For information-leaking Trojans, detection in the dormant state is critical, as once triggered, the secret data is already exfiltrated. This paper introduces a patch-based Transformer architecture for detecting dormant hardware Trojans through frequency-domain analysis of power traces. Our approach converts time-domain power measurements into frequency-domain representations using real Fast Fourier Transform (rFFT), revealing spectral signatures hidden in conventional time-series analysis. Experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves 90.94% average detection accuracy across dormant and active Trojan scenarios, outperforming state-of-the-art approaches particularly in detecting dormant Trojans that prior time-domain methods do not address.
tldr: This paper uses a patch-based Transformer with frequency-domain analysis to detect dormant hardware Trojans in integrated circuits via power side channels.
motivation: Hardware Trojans can leak sensitive information through power side channels, and detecting them in the dormant state is critical to prevent exfiltration.
method: The method converts time-domain power measurements to frequency-domain using real Fast Fourier Transform (rFFT) and applies a patch-based Transformer architecture for classification.
result: The approach achieves 90.94% average detection accuracy across dormant and active Trojan scenarios, outperforming prior time-domain methods.
conclusion: Frequency-domain analysis with patch-based Transformers effectively detects dormant hardware Trojans, addressing a gap in existing detection methods.

Atomic-scale details, especially those of disorder, are important for material properties, especially in semiconductors, but they are also extremely difficult to measure. Real-space methods can give direct access to this information, but typically, that access is limited. This review reports the application of three real-space techniques for measuring disorder to compound semiconductor materials: scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy. Where possible, it emphasizes cases in which the probes have been combined to achieve a more complete picture of the defects.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025006] Published Thu Jun 26, 2025.
tldr: This review covers atomic-scale microscopy techniques for measuring disorder in semiconductors, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding atomic-scale disorder is crucial for semiconductor material properties, but the paper focuses on materials characterization rather than quantum information processing.
method: The review discusses scanning tunneling microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom-probe microscopy applied to compound semiconductors.
result: The paper emphasizes combined use of these techniques to characterize defects and disorder at the atomic scale.
conclusion: The work is a materials science review with no relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Quantum Physics Of Stars
authors: M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. Deboer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, And A. Tumino
abstract:
Author(s): M. Wiescher, C. A. Bertulani, C. R. Brune, R. J. deBoer, A. Diaz-Torres, L. R. Gasques, K. Langanke, P. Navrátil, W. Nazarewicz, J. Okołowicz, D. R. Phillips, M. Płoszajczak, S. Quaglioni, and A. Tumino

There are many nuclear reactions that are of central importance for stellar burning and element formation. In typical stars, these reactions take place at very low energy, and many of them have very small rates, making it difficult to measure them directly in the laboratory. On the theoretical side, the low-energy regime is governed by quantum-mechanical phenomena like tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects. This review summarizes the state of the art in the theory of low-energy nuclear reactions in stars and describes new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025003] Published Tue May 27, 2025.
tldr: This paper reviews low-energy nuclear reactions in stars, focusing on quantum tunneling and resonances, but does not address quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Understanding nuclear reactions in stars is crucial for stellar burning and element formation, but the paper is purely nuclear physics without connection to the user's research interests.
method: The paper summarizes theoretical approaches to low-energy nuclear reactions, including quantum tunneling, near-threshold resonances, and interference effects.
result: It provides a state-of-the-art review of theoretical methods for stellar nuclear reactions.
conclusion: The paper concludes with new ideas for studying these reactions on Earth, but remains within nuclear astrophysics.

title: Codata Recommended Values Of The Fundamental Physical Constants: 2022
authors: Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, And Eite Tiesinga
abstract:
Author(s): Peter J. Mohr, David B. Newell, Barry N. Taylor, and Eite Tiesinga

This review contains the 2022 self-consistent set of values of the constants and conversion factors of physics and chemistry recommended by the Committee on Data for Science and Technology (CODATA). The CODATA values are based on a least-squares adjustment that takes into account all data available up to the end of 2022. Details of the data selection and methodology are described.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025002] Published Wed Apr 30, 2025.
tldr: This paper presents the 2022 CODATA recommended values of fundamental physical constants based on a least-squares adjustment of all available data.
motivation: Accurate and consistent values of fundamental constants are essential for science and technology, and periodic updates incorporate new measurements and improved uncertainties.
method: A least-squares adjustment is performed on a global dataset of measurements and theoretical calculations, taking into account correlations and uncertainties to produce self-consistent constant values.
result: The 2022 set of recommended values for fundamental constants and conversion factors is provided, with updated uncertainties compared to previous adjustments.
conclusion: The CODATA recommended values serve as the internationally accepted standard for fundamental constants, supporting precision measurements and theoretical work across physics and chemistry.

title: Gravitational GateWave: Gravitational Waves As Lfo Modulation Amplitude
authors: Carlos Dar\'io Badilla Cerdas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an audio gate plugin that uses real gravitational wave strain data from the LIGO and Virgo detectors as low frequency oscillator (LFO) modulation sources. Conventional audio gates rely on synthetic waveforms, sine, triangle, sawtooth, whose fixed harmonic content produces predictable pumping effects. By contrast, gravitational wave chirps from compact binary coalescences sweep through frequency and amplitude on subsecond timescales; when time scaled to LFO rates (0.1 to 10)Hz, these chirps yield modulation signals with continuously evolving harmonic structure. The plugin demonstrates that astrophysical signals can serve as musically compelling modulation sources, bridging sonification and creative audio processing.
tldr: This paper presents an audio gate plugin that uses real gravitational wave strain data as LFO modulation sources for creative audio processing.
motivation: To explore the use of astrophysical signals, specifically gravitational wave chirps, as musically compelling modulation sources in audio production.
method: The plugin takes gravitational wave strain data from LIGO/Virgo, time-scales it to LFO rates (0.1-10 Hz), and uses it to modulate an audio gate.
result: Gravitational wave chirps provide modulation signals with continuously evolving harmonic structure, offering a novel alternative to synthetic waveforms.
conclusion: Astrophysical signals can serve as creative modulation sources, bridging sonification and audio processing.

title: Gravitational DePhaser: A Temporal Gravitational Lensing Model For Creative Audio Processing
authors: Carlos Dar\'io Badilla Cerdas
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Classical delay, chorus, and reverb effects model multiple pro- pagation paths using discrete delays or statistical distributions. This work proposes a model inspired by gravitational lensing, where an audio signal is treated as a wave packet traversing a temporally distorted potential rather than physical spacetime. The distortion generates multiple effective propa- gation paths with different delays, phases, and gains, producing controlled constructive and destructive interference.
tldr: This paper proposes a creative audio processing model inspired by gravitational lensing, treating audio signals as wave packets in a temporally distorted potential.
motivation: To develop novel audio effects beyond classical delay, chorus, and reverb by leveraging concepts from gravitational lensing.
method: The model generates multiple effective propagation paths with different delays, phases, and gains by simulating a temporal gravitational potential, producing controlled interference.
result: The approach yields constructive and destructive interference patterns, enabling new creative audio processing capabilities.
conclusion: The gravitational lensing analogy provides a useful framework for designing innovative audio effects.

title: Combined Cavity Alignment And Mode-Mismatch Sensing Using Rf-qpd Sensors
authors: Stefan Ballmer Mitchell Schiworski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we describe a scheme for sensing both the mode mismatch and alignment of a cavity which does not require custom sensors and uses only Quadrant Photo-Detectors (QPDs). The technique is simple relying upon cylindrical lenses and thoughtful Gouy phase telescope design, and is trivial to implement alongside a Pound-Drever-Hall (PDH) locking scheme. The Gouy phase telescope design utilizes all three of the QPDs to sense each degree of freedom which also increases sensitivity and provides redundancy. The technique we show also works without RF modulation, which is useful for providing other general diagnostic information in complex optical experiments. An analytical overview of the technique as well as generic design equations for the Gouy phase telescope is provided. Finally, a detailed optical simulation is presented to verify the technique.
tldr: This paper presents a scheme for sensing cavity alignment and mode mismatch using quadrant photo-detectors and cylindrical lenses, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To simplify and improve the sensing of cavity alignment and mode mismatch in optical experiments without requiring custom sensors.
